💡 Key Takeaways
  • John Musker and Ron Clements' 1992 animated film "Aladdin" was one of the movies in the so-called Disney Renaissance, a period that was kicked off with the release of Disney's "The Little Mermaid" in 1989.
  • It has been revealed that "Aladdin," itself based on the classic tale from "One Thousand and One Nights," was a massive hit, earning $504 million at the box office.
  • (Infamously, Williams and Disney also come to loggerheads over the way "Aladdin" was marketed, but they ultimately settled the matter.).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

John Musker and Ron Clements' 1992 animated film "Aladdin" was one of the movies in the so-called Disney Renaissance, a period that was kicked off with the release of Disney's "The Little Mermaid" in 1989. That film's commercial and critical success revitalized the manufacturer from the doldrums it had been experiencing in the 1980s and led to a string of animated blockbusters, including "Beauty and the Beast" in 1991 and "Aladdin" in 1992.

It has been revealed that "Aladdin," itself based on the classic tale from "One Thousand and One Nights," was a massive hit, earning $504 million at the box office. The movie stars Robin Williams as the voice of the Genie, and having a celebrity at the center of a major animated feature was a novelty at the time. Not only that, casting Williams called for a complete reimagining of the Genie role, as the film would go on to retain the comedian's scattershot, improvisational comedy style.

(Infamously, Williams and Disney also come to loggerheads over the way "Aladdin" was marketed, but they ultimately settled the matter.).

In "Aladdin," the Genie adapts the guises of the various celebrities that Williams impersonates, among them Jack Nicholson, Ed Sullivan, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Rodney Dangerfield, and Groucho Marx. The comedy comes so fast and furious in "Aladdin" that one needs to watch the film several times to catch it all.

Recent findings suggest that case in point: After Aladdin (Scott Weinger) frees the Genie from his lamp, he is told, naturally, that he gets three wishes. Aladdin, however, isn't sure what to wish for, so he idly asks the Genie what he would wish for. It's then that Aladdin learns the Genie is really a prisoner of the lamp, with the latter memorably (and amusingly) describing himself as having "phenomenal cosmic power" but an "itty bitty living space.".

It's not the line itself that's funny, but Robin Williams' delivery, as well as the animation that matches it. He notes that being a prisoner is "part and parcel with the whole Genie gig." When he adds that he has "phenomenal cosmic powers," he rears up, turning red and arching his back into the heavens as cosmic storms thunder around him, his voice echoing. He then just as quickly shrinks down to a tiny size and folds himself bodily into his magical, hand-sized lamp before, explaining in a squeaky voice that he only has "itty bitty living space.".

Recent findings suggest that "Aladdin" later calls back to this line during its climax, at which point the wicked royal vizier Jafar (Jonathan Freeman) has taken control of the Genie and used his magic to become the most powerful sorcerer in the world. He then transforms into a giant snake and is about to squeeze Aladdin to death when the latter, thinking fast, teases Jafar that the Genie is still more powerful than he is. Knowing Aladdin is right, Jafar wishes to become a genie himself, not realizing he will now be enslaved to live inside a lamp himself. As Jafar disappears into his lamp, wailing in protest, Aladdin smirkingly points out that, yes, he, too, has phenomenal cosmic powers but itty bitty living space now. The battle has been won, and the heroes have triumphed.

According to recent reports, overall, this line is a funny way to describe the Genie's plight without making it sound too dark. He's a prisoner, but he stages it as a sad discomfort. "Aladdin" is a G-rated film that is appropriate for small children, so delving into the darkness of the Genie's enslavement isn't exactly something its creatives necessarily wanted to address.

The Genie cracks many a quotable line in "Aladdin," including the following:.

#120872. Guitarricadelafuente Was Terrified to Make His Acting Debut in ‘La Bola Negra’: ‘I Wasn’t Sure at All’

Guitarricadelafuente Was Terrified to Make His Acting Debut in ‘La Bola Negra’: ‘I Wasn’t Sure at All’

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2427 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • [Editor’s note: The following interview contains spoilers for “La Bola Negra.”].
  • Recent findings suggest that with a head of hair, lithe frame, and the soft eyes Caravaggio would’ve loved if the Italian painter were Spanish, pop star Guitarricadelafuente is having a monumental year on- and off-screen.
  • It has been revealed that oscar talk is in the wind, not just for his performance as queer closeted trumpeter Sebastián, who joins the Nationalist forces during the Spanish Civil War to survive, but for writing the original song “La Nieve.” The sweeping ballad ties together the film’s three story threads that convene around queer Spanish playwright Federico García Lorca’s incomplete text: 1932, 1937 (Sebastián’s storyline), and 2017.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

[Editor’s note: The following interview contains spoilers for “La Bola Negra.”].

Recent findings suggest that with a head of hair, lithe frame, and the soft eyes Caravaggio would’ve loved if the Italian painter were Spanish, pop star Guitarricadelafuente is having a monumental year on- and off-screen. The gay 29-year-old songwriter finished touring his sensational, sensually charged second album “Spanish Leather” earlier this fall, and only just a few short months after his screen debut, “La Bola Negra,” won a Cannes top prize, got scooped up by Netflix, and entered the awards season fray.

It has been revealed that oscar talk is in the wind, not just for his performance as queer closeted trumpeter Sebastián, who joins the Nationalist forces during the Spanish Civil War to survive, but for writing the original song “La Nieve.” The sweeping ballad ties together the film’s three story threads that convene around queer Spanish playwright Federico García Lorca’s incomplete text: 1932, 1937 (Sebastián’s storyline), and 2017. Born Álvaro Lafuente Calvo, he’s now a meme thanks to his stage and screen sobriquet, which means “little guitar of the fountain.” Related Stories ‘Hershey’ Review: An Unbelievably Flavorless Biopic About America’s Most Famous Chocolatier John Turturro, Carrie Coon, Guitarricadelafuente, and Peter Gamble to Receive SFFILM Honors.

In a recent development, guitarricadelafuente’s performance balances both hushed repression and eventually unleashed emotions throughout “La Bola Negra,” as Sebastián nurses wounded (and handsome) Republican soldier Rafael (Miguel Bernardeau, a more established actor in Spain). They fall for each other in the process, in a furtive romance mostly framed in stolen glances and tacit looks — in other words, the sort of good old-fashioned gay yearning that’s made movies like “Brokeback Mountain,” “Call Me by Your Name,” and “God’s Own Country” so popular. “La Bola Negra” is, by now, one of the highest-grossing Spanish movies ever to play in Spain, and it’s a major Oscar contender in select theaters as it gears up for its early December Netflix streaming premiere.

IndieWire spoke to Guitarricadelafuente over Zoom where, behind him, an oversized window frame flanked the waves gently rushing up to Miami Beach. Below, we discuss his songwriting process for “La Nieve,” witnessing the breakup of directors Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo (which happened during filming), and how he overcame his fears to make his auspicious screen debut. That’s all while balancing a proudly out music career where his sexuality is front and center. Plus, watch an exclusive video about his role in the film at the bottom of this story.

The following interview has been edited and condensed for clarity and length.

Industry observers note that indieWire: You’ve been all over the world with “La Bola Negra,” from Cannes in May to Toronto and, now, Miami Beach for this virtual junket interview. You’re used to being all over the place. You also toured your album this year. Did that help you prepare for promoting the film?

According to recent reports, guitarricadelafuente: I would say that kind of, in a way, because there’s something that I see as very similar to going and talking about the movie and talking about your character, which is something very similar to when you’re going around touring with your album. I think it’s more difficult because you need to talk about yourself and not just about playing a character because the music you make comes from a very profound place, and you need to talk about many things that go inside of you.

This is your acting debut, and there’s Oscar chatter for both your performance and the song you wrote for the film, “La Nieve.” Do you watch the Academy Awards in Spain?

In a recent development, not that much recently, but I remember when I was studying architecture in college, I used to stay up late at night doing projects. I remember staying up until 3:00 a.m. and with my friends, we were doing our little houses, and we would put the television on, and see the awards. But that was one of the only times that I stayed up late, or that I used to stay up late to see the awards, because you always receive that in Spain in the morning after.

You signed up for the movie without a script. What was the pitch that the Javis gave you? You knew you’d have to learn the trumpet.

In a recent development, they didn’t tell me that I had to learn an instrument because it was going to be originally something that I already knew how to play, but they wanted to make it more difficult. So they mentioned, “OK, why don’t you try a trumpet?” But yeah, the first pitch, there was not much about it. They told me about “La piedra oscura” by Alberto Conejero, which was the original play where the characters of Rafael and Sebastián appear.

Industry observers note that I just knew that it was going to be set against the backdrop of the Spanish Civil War, with Lorca being so present. … They didn’t convince me, but I was so moved by how they were so confident that I could do it because I was so frightened and I wasn’t sure at all, but it was their vision. I admired them so much from before. I knew that they’ve worked with many nonprofessional actors, and people acting for the first time. So it was something that I just threw myself into.

You were frightened about whether or not you could deliver as an actor, or was it the material?

I was spending all of my time making music and touring, and it was very time-consuming and exhausting. … I didn’t know if I could put myself into that experience because I thought the proper way to dig into that role was to put your soul into it.

According to recent reports, they were looking for someone who was openly gay for this role, right? There’s a spectrum of sexualities among the cast. Miguel Bernardeau, your scene partner, is straight.

It has been revealed that well, I don’t even know if we talked about that at any point because it was just assumed that I was. [Laughs] I don’t know if that was a condition. I think it was something that, to be more faithful to the story, had to happen. At the time that they approached me with the role, I was finishing my last album, “Spanish Leather.” It represented an imaginary — but not that imaginary — journey of a young gay man who comes out from his village and puts himself out to the world, discovering who he is and where he belongs.

Many people would know my music, but I would realize that not many people knew that I was gay even. There’s a big, not sexual, but I would say sensual component to [“Spanish Letter”] and this process of growing up and sexual [awakening]. So it was very special in a way to play this role … it’s something that you don’t get that much, maybe in Spain, just to see things where you can get referenced with or reflected with.

Los Javis broke up during production. Did they communicate that to the cast? How did you find out?

It was so weird because I don’t know if I’m stupid or what, I didn’t even notice. I would hear obviously so many rumors, but … you couldn’t tell that they were apart because they were acting as one. And I couldn’t believe that they were breaking up with the intensity of that shoot. It was like, “How on earth are they going to split up in the middle of this craziness and this madness?”.

But I don’t even remember when they told us. I think it was at the end of the shoot. We would eventually know that something was going on. I couldn’t believe it. How have you managed to carry this shoot? But that also represented how moving this story was to them.

People were gossiping at that point.

Sources indicate that of course. Even when they reached out to me with the role, I would hear rumors, and I was like, “How is this going to be possible if they’re so tight together?” It was inevitable because they are so well known in Spain, that rumors would arrive.

Miguel has probably 10 years of acting experience that you don’t have. Was he helpful as a mentor, as well as an onscreen romance?

According to recent reports, the first time that we met, it was actually when he was doing his audition because the only character that was clear in the movie was Sebastián. We had to test how this approach was going to be with the real Rafael, because this very tight and intimate connection had to happen. He didn’t know that I was going to play Sebastián, and he just appeared in the rehearsal room. And I thought there was a very special instant connection there, that I think we’re obviously very different, or we come from very different backgrounds or different ways of seeing the world.

Sources indicate that but there was a beauty in that because obviously I saw him as this wonderful, beautiful, talented, and professional actor that I could anchor myself in. He’s all the time lying on a bed [on screen]. And so he has to say so many things without being able to move. We were both left a lot of freedom on set and to try and to make errors. The room would get empty, and it was just Los Javis, Miguel, and I.

Were you writing the movie’s theme song, “La Nieve,” during production?

It was a very long process from the beginning, when I was told to write the song. I don’t think of me doing a song as in I get into a room and say, “OK, what I’m going to talk about right now?” And then I get a lyric, and I go back home. This Film has so many stories in it, and to try to be faithful to all of them and try to unify them in a thread, in a song, was very difficult. I was listening at the time, before they reached out to me, to Spanish Civil War songs.

In a recent development, it was actually a queer singer of the time who was called Rolando Alarcón. There were songs played with parlor guitars that were [made] to be sung on the waterfront. We started preparing the role with Los Javis. Lorca had to be very present also in this because he’s all over the place. He’s pretty omnipresent all of the time, surveilling what’s going on. And you had to pay a homage to him because, in the end, “La bola negra” was this unfinished script that he was writing.

I had to live my character in my own skin and properly carry that emotional baggage that he was holding. And it wasn’t until the end of the shoot, when we were in Cantabria living for two months … I obviously had this melody in my head, but when this scene with the firing squad happens, and [SPOILER ALERT] Rafael dies, it was a combination of all of that emotional journey that the character was living.

According to recent reports, I would arrive home that day and start playing a melody on a piano and mumbling some lyrics, and I would send this to Los Javis, and I didn’t know that they were going to use this to unify the three stories that go on in the movie. And it was a way for me to let all of that emotion go.

Recent findings suggest that this song will now have to be part of every setlist you perform. It’s your “My Heart Will Go On.”.

In a recent development, I hope it turns into that. I wish to be 50 years old and be in Madrid and be singing that. That would be so beautiful. Because I feel that I was just playing in Madrid my last concert one month ago, it was kind of the closing chapter of this “Spanish Leather” tour, and the film was just released one week before that. And so I got the chance to play “La Nieve” there for the first time. After that, it was very emotional because you would hear 18,000 people singing to that. It was like goosebumps. After that, people would be commenting on TikTok, “So Sebastián had the chance to finally be a musician and get to Madrid and perform.” That’s kind of like a closing of the thread, a very beautiful thing.

Industry observers note that “La Bola Negra” is also one of the highest-grossing Spanish movies to play in Spain ever. Have you been able to go home and experience that?

Recent findings suggest that we were in Spain those first two weeks until we had the last concert in Madrid, and then we went to Toronto and all over the place. And that was a very special week because I was at my sister’s wedding. You could feel something in the air. There was a communal excitement, and people of all ages, all different ages, going to the cinema, or even people, like aunts of mine, who haven’t been to the cinema in 10 years, to see how that’s happening is something that makes us very proud.

For me, the Spanish premiere was more important because that’s all Spanish people’s lives. Everybody has been linked to that moment of time, it’s like their ancestors. So the Spanish were going to be the most critical of it. But to see how young people, old people, people from different backgrounds go and you suddenly have this sense of communion was something spectacular that you could see in the streets. Like older ladies and young queer guys coming up to you, it’s just incredible.

What are you doing next? Do you want to keep acting?

Yeah. It’s been a crazy time. I’m having the time to even make latest music and to, I don’t know, to see what I’m able to, because even three years ago… I would oblige myself to be quiet and rest to be able to feel inspired. But now it’s all these hectic times that are making me feel so inspired, and to share that time and put it into making art.

“La Bola Negra” is now in select theaters will start streaming on Netflix on Wednesday, December 2.

These 14 Upcoming Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1483 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov.
  • Sources indicate that technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program.
  • The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the organization's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov. 3. While this update isn't as large as iOS 27 proper, it's surprisingly feature-filled for a 0.3 update. This is only a beta, so anything could (and likely will) change before Apple officially launches the update. But, as it stands, iOS 27.3 tests 10 fresh features—including one feature the company trialed in the previous beta.

Sources indicate that technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program. But a word of warning: Betas can be temperamental, and could be risky. As such, I'd recommend avoiding the beta until Apple releases the public beta, which comes after a bit more testing to iron out larger issues. Either way, make sure to make a full backup of your iPhone to a Mac or PC first, as issues with the beta could result in permanent data loss.

The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the organization's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID. While it works well enough for unlocking your iPhone, it's still an adjustment for those of us used to Face ID. With iOS 27.3, Apple is now testing face unlock for the Duo—not Face ID, mind you. The Duo's front camera doesn't have the tech required to power Face ID or its secure protocols. Instead, this feature simply unlocks your iPhone Duo with a face scan. In addition, your Duo will still require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. You can read more about this new feature here.

It has been revealed that iOS 27.3 also comes with a upcoming setting that lets you lock your iPhone Duo by closing it—as you would expect from, say, a laptop—or, dare I say, a flip phone? Presently, closing the Duo seamlessly transitions what's on the big screen to the smaller display, and you have to press the side button to lock the phone.

According to recent reports, with watchOS 27, Apple released "Audio Intelligence," a fresh set of features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Audio Intelligence uses the watches' new S11 chip, along with on-device AI and cloud-based AI, to run new features, like Sound Recognition and Shazam (music recognition).

In a recent development, with iOS 27.3, however, the firm is now officially testing the other two Audio Intelligence features it originally announced with watchOS 27. First, there's Live Rewind: By double-clicking the watch crown, you can pull up a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. Siri Recap, on the other hand, displays summaries of conversations you had that day, in case you need a refresher on any chats you might have otherwise forgotten about,.

The company generated some controversy when it first announced these two Audio Intelligence features, since, on the surface, it sounds like these new Apple Watches are essentially spying on people all day long. According to Apple, however, that isn't really the case. The company states Audio Intelligence is private, and never records or stores any audio. No speakers are ever identified, and text results (both transcripts and summaries) are deleted automatically after a set period of time unless the user saves them to the Siri app. You can read more about how Audio Intelligence works here.

According to recent reports, despite their claims, I'm sure there will still be strong feelings surrounding these Audio Intelligence features. We'll have to see whether Apple can prove Live Rewind and Siri Recap aren't all that creepy throughout the iOS 27.3 beta process.

iOS 27.3 also introduces app actions for Siri AI. Apple is testing newly introduced abilities for Siri AI, including organizing files, planning events, or adding photos to albums. You could ask Siri to organize your Downloads folder, or delete files that haven't been opened in more than a year. You could ask Siri to find a coffee shop you went to last week, or to save an article to your Reading List in Safari. You could ask Siri to check your calendar and set up a time for an event based on when you're free. You can even ask the assistant to schedule, edit, or unsend messages.

Sources indicate that for example, you could ask Siri AI to help you plan a trip with your friends. You could ask the AI to put together a themed playlist in Apple Music, schedule a message to a group about an upcoming trip, organize the websites you've been visiting in Safari into a tab group, and, after the trip, ask Siri to move your best photos to your favorites album. These newly introduced actions work in the following apps: Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. Developers can also add Siri AI app actions support to their own apps.

According to recent reports, apple started testing its fresh Health app with the iOS 27.2 beta, but pulled the redesign before the official release. Now, with iOS 27.3, the new app is back. The new Health app has a health dashboard for the first time, as well as new features like Health Age and movement assessments. It seems to be pulling from some popular competitor services, hopefully, for the better. For more on the new Health app, check out Lifehacker health editor Beth Skwarecki's explainer.

It has been revealed that continuing on the Health track, iOS 27.3 also introduces "Gym Strength." This is a new Fitness+ feature that offers a personalized four-week strength-training initiative. You can customize these intends to meet your goals, experience level, and schedule, and they adapt as you progress. You'll get recommendations based on your experience with exercises, reps, and sets, including video demos for exercises. You can access Gym Strength on both iPhone and iPad, and Apple Watches are optional—though you can log your progress with the wearable if you have it.

Apple is also testing a latest Siri AI feature in Safari, that gives the bot access to entire webpages, including the parts of the site that aren't on-screen. Say you want to know all the gluten-free options on a menu on a restaurant's website, but only a portion of the site is actually in view. You could ask Siri to read you the gluten-free options, and it would pull from the whole page, even though you can only see part of it.

Vertical tabs have been a favorite among browser aficionados, as they give you more screen real estate in your browser while keeping your tabs off the side. Apple hasn't made the jump—until now. This feature works with iPads running iPadOS 27.3 as well as Macs running macOS 27.3.

Another upcoming Safari feature in testing is "Adaptive Dark Mode." This feature forces websites into a dark theme, if they don't have a native theme of their own. There are third-party apps that can do this, but this is the first time Apple has offered this feature built into Safari.

Apple is also testing new StandBy experiences with iOS 27.3, which were previously only available on the iPhone Duo. When you turn your iPhone sideways while plugged in, you'll find new Analog and Digital Clock faces with new customization options. There's also a new Photos face, with the option to pull images from Shared Albums.

"Reachability" pulls your iPhone's display down towards the bottom of the screen, so you can access items towards the top of the display with one hand. It's a useful feature for those of us with massive iPhones, and now, there's no iPhone bigger than the Duo. With iOS 27.3, Apple is testing Reachability for its first foldable phone. It's a bit like the inverse of how Reachability currently works: You can swipe on the left or right side of your Duo's display to shift the other side of the screen towards your current position. If you're holding your Duo in your left hand, a swipe of the left side will pull the right side over to the left, and vice versa.

Apple is also rolling out upcoming languages for Siri AI in iOS 27.3. Now, Apple's smart assistant supports Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

According to recent reports, if you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPad running iPadOS 27.3, you now have access to Siri Mode in Camera. As with iOS, you can open the Camera app on iPadOS to access Siri Mode, and ask Siri about your surroundings.

It has been revealed that if you watch videos in Apple Podcasts, you can find them in more sources than the Podcasts app. With the new updates, you'll find these videos on Apple TV 4K, select smart TVs, your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and even in CarPlay. (Please don't watch video podcasts while driving.).

#120870. The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth Credits Scene Explained: What Happens To Brad Pitt's Cliff?

The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth Credits Scene Explained: What Happens To Brad Pitt's Cliff?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (903 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This article contains spoilers for "The Further MIs-Adventures of Cliff Booth.".
  • According to recent reports, 2019's "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" concluded with a magic trick only the movies could provide.
  • It has been revealed that "Cliff Booth" ends on an ambiguous note.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article contains spoilers for "The Further MIs-Adventures of Cliff Booth.".

According to recent reports, 2019's "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" concluded with a magic trick only the movies could provide. In Quentin Tarantino's depiction of Los Angeles circa August, 1969, the real-life murder of actress Sharon Tate (Margot Robbie) and others by members of the Manson Family is averted thanks to the intervention of fictional actor Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and his stunt double buddy Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt). In essence, it's an ending in which movie magic takes over real life. The semi-sequel to "Hollywood," "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth," reaches a conclusion that's similar in function but disparate in tone. Instead of life-imitating-cinema acting as savior, it's a death knell for poor Cliff. Or is it?

It has been revealed that "Cliff Booth" ends on an ambiguous note. After spending much of the film attempting to quell a dispute between the blowhard insecure actor Charlie Peters (Scott Caan) and a pair of Filipino gangsters, Eddie and Fernando Verdusco (Matt Groove and JB Tadena, respectively), Cliff arranges a clandestine meeting between the brothers and himself at a bar in Hollywood. This meeting deliberately mirrors a similar encounter at the beginning of the film, in which Cliff has a couple of other ne'er do wells meet him at the Fresh Beverly Theater, a meeting which ends with Cliff's triumph. Cliff is similarly cocksure going into his meeting with the Verduscos, but things promptly and violently get out of hand. He does manage to kill both gangsters, but at the expense of himself being burned alive and (possibly) mortally wounded.

For the film, Tarantino has handed over the directing reins to David Fincher, and this ending is a perfect summation of Fincher's mean-spirited satire, a final moment which is either Cliff's lowest point or the bitter end of his story.

Throughout his career, David Fincher has enjoyed making films in which his protagonists undergo a great deal of suffering. This doesn't always mean that they're deserving of such suffering, but Fincher does tend to have more dark, mean-spirited fun with those who are: Jack in "Fight Club," Mark Zuckerberg in "The Social Network," and the titular assassin in "The Killer" are all good examples of such. Cliff in "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" can be added to this roster, though Fincher (via writer Quentin Tarantino) is a little more affectionate toward him than some of the others.

According to recent reports, the film begins with Cliff projecting the fictional Blaxploitation movie "Soul Brothers Die Hard," which he clearly loves enough to have memorized some dialogue from it. The climactic line uttered by the movie's lead is, "This don't mean s**t to me," which the character says as he's bleeding out amidst a fiery blaze.

The rest of the film sees Cliff saunter through his charmed life as a jack of all trades, gallivanting from a bartending job to a demolition derby appearance. He even gets recognized by a married couple for his moonlighting work as a porn star. He's essentially treated as an underground living legend of Hollywood, a near-mythic tough guy figure who nearly lives up to his larger-than-life persona. Yet when the Verdusco brothers violence erupts, Cliff loses control of the situation. The film smash cuts to credits as the bar the barely-alive Cliff is in rapidly catches fire, and then cuts back mid-credits to reveal Cliff, technically still alive but still stuck bleeding in the burning building, saying "This don't mean s**t to me." Reel life has become real life for the man, and it's all caught up with him.

If "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" is ultimately a fairy tale look at films and the film industry with some rough edges to it, "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is the inverse, a cold satire of Hollywood and its productions which has a silver lining of affection. At the center of the film is a discussion between Cliff, Charlie, his wife Toni (Carla Gugino), and Charlie's agent (and Cliff's love interest) Karen Crosby (Elizabeth Debicki), who originally worked as a film critic. Karen argues that cinema is placating entertainment that can never be considered true art. In Tarantino terms, this is another instance where his characters indulge in pop culture debate, and this depiction is never intended as either endorsement or derision (after all, he's had everyone from unrepentant killers to literal Nazis wax poetic on the movies and TV they love).

Industry observers note that however, for Fincher, this moment feels like thematic setup for the film's audience unfriendly, brutal, mean ending, in which our lovable (if morally questionable) hero loses. If Tarantino "purchased" the history-changing salvation of Sharon Tate in "Hollywood" through cinematic revisionism, then Fincher is using "Cliff Booth" as the payment due, a check written by Booth's part in saving Sharon as well as by him leaning into his own legend.

To be fair, we don't actually see Cliff die, so the ending could be seen as more sardonic. Yet its connection to the finality of "Soul Brothers Die Hard" along with the tropes of pulp and exploitation films (even Tarantino's "The Hateful Eight," too) heavily imply that Cliff isn't making it out of that bar alive. It's not a happy end, but it's a fitting one for Cliff to go out in a blaze of almost-glory.

And I liked his attention to detail around his understanding of the team, so I really adopted that.

It has been revealed that I think it’s absolutely crucial to be close to those people, and not in a disingenuous way. But when you see actors getting awards, like when they thank the crew, you totally understand that because you’re nothing as an island on a production.".

Although she might've recently returned — albeit with so much mystery surrounding the twist — Piper's original exit from Doctor Who remains one of the modern show's saddest moments. But why did she choose to leave after two seasons aboard the TARDIS? Although she "knew after two seasons" that her time was up, she was "wanting to leave after Season 1," Piper told Nemiroff. "Mostly, that was a bit reactive because Chris [Eccleston] was leaving and that felt quite destabilizing, but I wanted to move on with what I wanted to play. "I didn’t want to be on a family show anymore. I really didn’t like the feeling of the role model responsibility. I didn’t like how famous it made me, again, in the UK, having done my teens as a singer. So, it was a really easy decision for me. So, it sort of was irrelevant what other people stated.

Great in theory, but the ‘Smart’ part of Smart Reply struggled to materialize in iOS 18.

Smart Reply in Mail and Messages can now draw on a user’s personalized writing style.

According to recent reports, in iOS 18, I almost never used Smart Reply. That’s because despite being fine at suggesting replies that technically worked, those suggestions didn’t sound like me at all.

According to recent reports, the only drawback is that right now, you’ll only ever see two Smart Reply suggestions. If Apple expanded the feature by letting you scroll horizontally through more options, I suspect I’d use Smart Reply even more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, countless indicates have tried to recreate the magic of True Detective season 1, but only Apple TV’s spiritual successor made the smart choice to simply bring back its stars. To say that a lot of shows were influenced by 2014’s True Detective season 1 would be an egregious understatement. When the moody crime thriller debuted in 2014, True Detective swiftly became the most influential TV murder mystery since ABC’s iconic Twin Peaks.

Much like Twin Peaks helped pave the way for an entire genre of supernatural procedurals, including The X-Files, Buffy the Vampire Slayer, the still underrated Fox series Fringe, Supernatural, Evil, Lucifer, and Grimm, True Detective season 1 had almost as many imitators over the years. The show’s blend of southern gothic atmosphere, dual timeline storytelling, and brooding, bleak character study shaped countless cop dramas that followed.

From the horror-tinged atmosphere of His & Hers, Sharp Objects, and The Outsider to the dark, grounded storytelling of true-crime demonstrates like Mindhunter, Under the Bridge, and Under the Banner of Heaven, True Detective’s influence can be seen everywhere. Even more realistic crime dramas like HBO’s Mare of Easttown and Long Bright River owe something to the series, despite later seasons of True Detective failing to live up to season 1. However, none of these shows came as close to recapturing its appeal as Apple TV’s very, very different Brothers.

According to recent reports, in True Detective season 1, co-stars Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson play the mismatched cops Rust Cohle and Marty Hart, whose multi-decade working relationship sees both men driven to the brink of madness by an unsolved human trafficking ring. Their shared story is dark, brutal, and deeply compelling, but there are hints of deadpan humor to lighten the mood from time to time.

Anyone who saw those rare sardonic lines and thought that the pair really needed to star in a knockabout, lightweight comedy will be delighted to hear that is exactly what Brothers provides. Based on the bizarre real-life realization that Harrelson and McConaughey could be actual brothers due to their parents crossing paths by chance, Brothers follows fictionalized versions of the duo putting their friendship at risk when they live together on McConaughey’s ranch home.

While Brothers has a lot of fun with the idea that the two might unexpectedly be related, the show also gets a lot of its biggest laughs out of their similar screen and public personae. After all, both Harrelson and McConaughey are known for being laid-back southern charmers with a playful sense of humor and a rebellious streak, which initially made their True Detective casting seem unlikely.

In a recent development, while it might be hard to believe now, since both actors immersed themselves completely in the characters of Marty and Rust, there was a time when True Detective’s lead actors seemed too similar to work well together in a show about mismatched cops. Brothers trades on this by getting the pair to play less than flattering caricatures of themselves, who do indeed eventually find that both their similarities and differences grate on each other over time.

Industry observers note that with an astounding supporting cast including Natalie Martinez, Brittany Ishibashi, Holland Taylor, Lisa Gilroy, Skyler Gisondo, and Kevin Daniels, Brothers is undoubtedly a fun watch. Admittedly, many of the show’s reviews noted that its sparse premise might have been better served with a movie-length runtime, something that has become an increasingly common problem in the streaming era.

Industry observers note that however, for fans of the two stars, this comedy is a must-watch. Even though countless highlights have copied various elements of True Detective season 1’s formula, it somehow took until 2026 for Apple TV’s comedy Brothers to make the ingenious move of ignoring the entire style, story, and tone of the show and simply reuniting its stars.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the star of this year's Resident Evil adaptation endured another horrific experience in the thriller Whalefall in October, which put actor Austin Abrams inside the belly of a 60-ton sperm whale in a fight for survival. While that situation sounds harrowing in real life, filming scenes simulating being inside a whale's stomach also looks exhausting. In a new exclusive clip from Whalefall, viewers get a peek behind the scenes at what Abrams experienced, as more than a dozen stomach puppeteers recreated the visceral action of being digested — all while your host is being attacked by killer whales.

Sources indicate that in Whalefall, Abrams' character Jay Gardiner goes on a solo dive, only to be attacked by a giant squid, which is in turn consumed by the 80-foot sperm whale. As the squid and Jay are being chewed up, the experienced-but-reckless diver grapples with grief (unrelated to being eaten) while also trying to escape his fleshy prison.

To believably create that survival scenario, the production team at Wētā Workshop created four different stomach sets that could be jostled, climbed, and filled with goop simulating digestive juices. “It was super notable that Austin felt like he was in these environments and his body had to respond to them,” Whalefall production designer Ramsey Avery told Polygon in a virtual interview. “All that motion on camera is motion that we’re making. It’s not animated. That means Austin’s body is responding to real action in real time.”.

Ben Milsom, on-set supervisor for Wētā Workshop, explains in a upcoming behind-the-scenes clip that the stomachs had to accommodate filming, but also violently move and behave like a real whale's stomach. "This is a character in the movie not just a set," Milsom indicates. "It has to move. It has to have personality." That required between 14 and 16 people to work simultaneously to make the stomach move and breathe, Milsom says.

Whalefall will be released on digital platforms on Dec. 1. A physical release on Blu-ray and 4K Ultra HD is coming Jan. 12, 2027.

Playing Bond does not lend an actor cred with the Academy. But it does extend a career.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home. The only carve-out is lighting, because some rooms are hard to judge by time of day alone. Depending on the windows and placement against the sun, some rooms might need light-based automations earlier in the day than others. The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes that with a light sensor most motion sensors lack, along with mmWave radar.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

Industry observers note that A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations. If you’re still for long periods, you’re invisible, and the automation assumes the room is empty. The Lafaer LWR02 pairs PIR with 2.4 GHz mmWave radar. The PIR-based motion sees you walking in, and the radar sees the minor stuff, like breathing and shifting on the couch, so the room stays “occupied” for as long as you are in it. The two together also reduce false positives from ceiling fans, curtains, and the dog, because the radar and PIR both must agree before the sensor reports motion.

In Apple Home, that reveals up as an occupancy sensor and a motion sensor from the same device.

Recent findings suggest that “Turn on the lights when someone enters” is a common automation I use, but it can be tricky. What if you only want it when it’s not light outside? Doing it based on time of day sometimes works, but what about depending on where the windows are facing, etc.? You might have a room that gets darker an hour earlier than another room. “Turn on the lights when someone enters, and it’s dark in the room” is what the light sensor can handle for you.

Recent findings suggest that in the Home app, that means triggering a sensor for occupancy, then converting the automation into a Shortcut and adding a condition for the light level. It’s a few extra steps, but it does really give you more fine control over how it works.

Presence, motion, light, temperature, and humidity all come from the same device, and each one appears in Apple Home as its own sensor, so you can build automations around whichever ones fit the room.

It’s IPX3-rated, so bathrooms, kitchens, and laundry rooms are fine to use in. Coverage is about 13 feet for presence and 26 for motion across about 120 degrees, which works in a bedroom, office, or bathroom. It’s not going to cover a great room from one corner. The base is a magnetic half sphere, so you can aim it, and it mounts with adhesive or sits on a shelf. I generally like to use the shelf for these types of sensors.

Sources indicate that the Lafaer LWR02 is Matter over Thread, so it pairs directly with a HomePod, HomePod mini, or Apple TV 4K with no Lafaer hub or account needed. It runs on two included AAA batteries, is rated for up to two years, and rechargeable AAAs work with it as well. Thread is why a sensor doing this much can last that long on batteries. All sensor data is processed locally, so it only uses a trickle on the batteries.

According to recent reports, lights that turn off while you’re sitting still in the room are the reason a lot of people stop using motion automations in smart homes. The Lafaer LWR02 fixes that with mmWave radar and then lets you have more granular control of light-based automations based on what’s actually in the environment in the room, not just the time of day.

The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor is available on Amazon.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that "Welcome to a future we no longer control." So says the official tagline for the Prime Video series "Blade Runner 2099," which is set (self-evidently) 50 years after the events of Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049" movie.
  • It has been revealed that not that we'll actually see any of that go down within "Blade Runner 2099," mind you.
  • "To be honest, I feel like I've seen that before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that "Welcome to a future we no longer control." So says the official tagline for the Prime Video series "Blade Runner 2099," which is set (self-evidently) 50 years after the events of Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049" movie. The world has undergone some seriously seismic changes since then, as viewers will quickly realize in the opening moments of the show. Where both Ridley Scott's classic 1982 film "Blade Runner" and Villeneuve's 2017 sequel took place under very traditional confines (with humanity ruling over bioengineered Replicants as second-class citizens), "2099" has flipped the script entirely. Instead, the Replicants have orchestrated a full-scale uprising and seized control.

It has been revealed that not that we'll actually see any of that go down within "Blade Runner 2099," mind you. The series premiere opens well after this revolutionary turn of events has become old news. It's a bold and decisive creative choice, and one that I had to ask showrunner Silka Luisa about during a recent press junket. Why set this story in the aftermath of such a development rather than during it? As she tells it, it had to do with telling a story we haven't already seen in pop culture before:.

"To be honest, I feel like I've seen that before. Not with Replicants, but definitely the robot revolution is definitely something I can close my eyes and picture. It's been in the zeitgeist and people have done different takes on it, so it didn't seem like I was going to be putting anything out into the world that people couldn't imagine for themselves.".

Reading between the lines, it's true that properties like "Terminator" have already covered this ground before. And, in fairness, a wartime drama wouldn't quite mesh with the neo-noir vibes of "Blade Runner." But, for Luisa, her reasons extend even deeper than that.

Considering the timeline established in "Blade Runner" and "2049," the Replicant uprising in "Blade Runner 2099" has been almost a century in the making. The Denis Villeneuve sequel even took steps to directly integrate this possibility into its plot, keeping a Replicant rebellion simmering in the background of its story. In the Prime Video series, this powder keg has been detonated, and now the various characters (including Michelle Yeoh's Replicant Blade Runner Olwen and Hunter Schafer's incognito human Cora) have to live with the consequences.

According to Silka Luisa, this was a challenge that she embraced from the start. It's fairly easy to tell a straightforward story about revolution, but it's much harder to depict what comes next. As she told me over Zoom, "Whereas, what I really wasn't sure about myself at the beginning and that was interesting, was what happens afterwards. What does it look like to lose? And if you have been disempowered for your entire existence, what do you do with power?".

According to recent reports, it's a fascinating question to pose to a group of sentient beings frequently described as "more human than human." They make look, walk, and bleed like humans ... but Replicants have always been designed to be far stronger, physically. When the oppressed throw off their shackles, do they then become the oppressors in turn? According to Luisa:.

In a recent development, "Those were just, at least to me personally, much more interesting questions than just a simple idea of which side is gonna win. When, in truth, you kind of know which side is gonna win [laughs].".

All eight episodes of "Blade Runner 2099" are right now streaming on Prime Video.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, mike Plante, a filmmaker and 25-year veteran of the Sundance Institute, died Tuesday after a brief illness. He was 56.

At Sundance, Plante worked as a Shorts Programmer and was a familiar, warm-hearted presence at festival screenings and events.

“Mike was a treasure to the Institute, the Festival, and our independent film community,” Sundance Festival Director Eugene Hernandez and Director of Programming Kim Yutani said in a joint statement. “His sense of wonder and humor were matched by boundless enthusiasm and curatorial excellence. Our Festival’s Short Film Program and the Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour were shaped by Mike’s energy and superb taste in movies. Mike’s roots at Sundance Institute, and his relationships within our organization and festival, run deep. He will be remembered and deeply missed as a true cinephile, a filmmaker, a champion of short films, movie theaters, and film culture.” Related Stories Will Robert Pattinson’s Bond Casting Help Land Him His First Oscar Nomination? Guitarricadelafuente Was Terrified to Make His Acting Debut in ‘La Bola Negra’: ‘I Wasn’t Sure at All’.

In addition to his work at the festival, Plante directed the 2011 feature documentary “Be Like an Ant,” which followed a Vietnam War veteran who builds a house around a mobile home to handle winter living. He also directed numerous shorts including “The Polaroid Job” (2016), which looked at his parents’ work running a paid event-photography studio in the 1980s. It is available to watch on the New York Times’ Op-Doc website.

Recent findings suggest that amy Redford, the daughter of Sundance founder Robert Redford and a board member of the festival, called Plante, “a visionary.” “Through his extraordinary curatorial talent, he launched countless storytellers through the vital medium of short film, many of whom have gone on to become some of the world’s most enduring artists,” she said. “Mike embodied the Sundance ethos and played a critical role in preserving the continuity of its values. He was unfailingly generous with his time and mentorship, and a talented creator in his own right. But Mike’s most enduring legacy is his kindness. It was, and remains, the first thing people say about him. His passing is a profound loss not only to the Sundance community, but to all those fortunate enough to have known and loved him. He will be deeply missed.”.

Along with directing, Plante produced feature documentaries by other directors, including “Scrap Vessel” (2009) and “Giuseppe Makes A Movie” (2014). Plante started working for film festivals as a programmer in 1993, eventually joining Sundance in 2001.

Sources indicate that in 1998, he started the film zine Cinemad, which he wrote for and produced a podcast. The site championed indie and under-seen movies. Plante also wrote “Sensation Cinema: The Audacious, Defiant History of Louis Sher and the Art Theatre Guild,” which looked at an influential arthouse theater owner and distributor. It was a world that Plante knew intimately. In 2024, he was named head of distribution at The Beverly Theater, an independent cinema in Las Vegas, Nevada. He also worked with the CineVegas Film Festival with Trevor Groth, another Sundance vet, as its Director of Programming.

Plante is survived by his mother, Barb.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The holiday shopping season is here, and Apple’s AirPods are sure to be one of the most popular gifts. If you’re shopping for AirPods, Apple sells three different models: AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2. Here’s how they compare.

According to recent reports, airPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions. Unlike their predecessors, both versions of AirPods 5 offer Active Noise Cancellation. They differ in the charging case, battery life, and volume control. The base model AirPods 5 ($129) come with a case that can only charge via USB-C.

The case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My. You also get one extra hour of battery life. The higher-end model also adds on-stem volume control, so you can adjust the volume just by swiping up or down on one of the earbud stems.

Here’s a full comparison between both AirPods 5 models:.

In a recent development, the key thing about AirPods 5 is their open-ear design, unlike the in-ear design of the AirPods Pro 3 (more on those later). Even with that open-ear design, AirPods 5 offer incredible Active Noise Cancellation capabilities.

It has been revealed that if you are shopping for AirPods 5, I do recommend spending the extra $20 to get the higher-end model. The better charging case alone is worth the extra money. With Find My integration and a built-in speaker, you can track your AirPods and play a sound from the case if you lose them.

If the person you’re shopping for doesn’t like in-ear earbuds, AirPods 5 are an excellent choice.

For most people, though, AirPods Pro 3 are probably the better choice ….

Industry observers note that airPods Pro 3 are Apple’s most capable earbuds, even with the introduction of AirPods 5 this year. They offer an in-ear fit and come with five foam-infused silicone ear tip sizes. With that in-ear design, AirPods Pro 3 can offer up to 3x stronger noise cancellation than AirPods 5. In my testing, this difference is notable.

AirPods Pro 3 also offer several other features you won’t find on AirPods 5, including a heart rate sensor for workouts, plus Hearing Test, Hearing Aid, and Hearing Protection features.

Industry observers note that I still think AirPods Pro 3 are one of the best products in Apple’s lineup today. I wear mine for multiple hours every single day and can’t imagine life without them. I love the in-ear fit, and the ANC still impresses me, whether I’m at home or somewhere like a coffee shop.

If you know the person you’re shopping for (whether it’s yourself or someone else) likes the in-ear earbud design, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option. This is especially true when AirPods Pro 3 are on sale, like they are right now at $149. The price difference between AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 is very small, and you’re getting a much better product.

Finally, we have AirPods Max. These are Apple’s only option for people who want AirPods in an over-ear headphone form factor. Last year, they were pretty hard to recommend since they’d gone five years without a real upgrade.

This year, however, Apple officially introduced AirPods Max 2, bringing modern features to Apple’s high-end headphones. This includes features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Volume, and more.

AirPods Max 2 are a far more compelling option than AirPods Max were at this time last year. They’re still pricey, but I love the aesthetics and find them very comfortable. There’s something about the premium aluminum design with an elegant Digital Crown that really stands out.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking to splurge this holiday season, AirPods Max 2 are a great choice. For more realistic budgets, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that with the release of the final two episodes of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3, Sauron (Charlie Vickers) has finally crafted his One Ring to Rule Them All.
  • The Rings of Power's opening credits have told the story of Middle-earth, leading to the Second Age, through sound.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Editor's note: The below contains spoilers for The Rings of Power Season 3 Episode 7.

Recent findings suggest that with the release of the final two episodes of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3, Sauron (Charlie Vickers) has finally crafted his One Ring to Rule Them All. This moment has been years in the making, and although the other Rings of Power have already made their way to the screen, the One Ring brings this prequel one step closer to J.R.R. Tolkien's original high-fantasy tale. But while the Prime Video series has only just unveiled the Dark Lord's secret weapon, The Rings of Power has teased the One Ring's creation from the very beginning.

The Rings of Power's opening credits have told the story of Middle-earth, leading to the Second Age, through sound. Set to a song composed by Howard Shore, the intro uses cymatics to mold and transform swirling particles, recounting the events of creation as conducted by Eru Ilúvatar through the Music of the Ainur. This eventually leads, as the Season 1 opening credits depict, to the creation of the nine rings of Men, seven for the Dwarves, and three for the Elves, along with Sauron's master ring itself. Season 2's intro does something similar. Although the credits themselves change each season, with the sand and dust forming different (and timely) constructs with every renovation, the process itself remains the same. In fact, it's in this process of visual sound that Sauron forges his own Ring of Power.

It has been revealed that in the penultimate episode of Season 3, Sauron crafts the long-anticipated One Ring, a moment that has been teased since the series first began. As the Dark Lord works in the fires of Mount Doom, he uses Fëanor's hammer — stolen from Celebrimbor (Charles Edwards) — to strike the anvil containing his forging materials (gold and silver from Valinor), creating a massive vibration throughout the volcano. As the shock wave hits the walls of the mountain and falls back, each blast shapes the particles, eventually forming the Ring itself before Sauron imbues it with his dark power. The visual similarities are evident in the way the soot and dirt shift and move, and though it's not as seamless or smooth as the opening credits, it's most certainly by design.

Recent findings suggest that if the slipping and swirling sands in the opening credits are meant to echo the work of the angelic Ainur themselves, then Sauron's frantic, angry, and desperate attempts take a clunkier, less polished approach. Indeed, there's a reason why he argues with the ghost of Celebrimbor — be it in his own warped mind or a genuine appreciation, it makes no difference — in his quest to forge the master ring. Unlike the Ainur, he is not so naturally in tune with creation that he can properly sub-create such a simple vessel of power, and this is clear in the Season 3 credits themselves, which are more explosive and expansive regarding the borders of Mordor than they are life-giving and generative, focusing solely on the One Ring at the expense of all else.

While The Rings of Power depicts the One Ring's forging at the end of Season 3, Tolkien originally wrote it occurring at a different point in time. As detailed in The Silmarillion, Sauron first deceived the Elves into forging rings for Men and Dwarves under the guise of Annatar, Lord of Gifts. He aided Celebrimbor in the making of these initial 16 rings, but left Eregion to forge the One Ring in secret, leaving the smith to craft the three Elven rings on his own. These rings, on the Elves' part, were, per Tolkien's description in correspondence collected in The Letters of J.R.R. Tolkien, made to prevent the "decay" of Middle-earth. Since Sauron had no hand in making them, they were left unmarred, but the moment Sauron put on his master ring, the Elves became keenly aware of the deception and removed their rings. We see this occur in The Rings of Power Season 3's penultimate episode as well.

Unlike the Prime Video series, the exact details of Sauron's forging are left unknown. However, it's quite doubtful he needed to ask a Balrog to master the secrets that he, having studied under Aulë, Smith of the Valar, already knew and imparted to others in the forging of the other rings. While the One Ring was meant to rule the others, it was certainly within his own ability to craft. Sauron also imbued it with his own fëa (the Quenya word for "soul") and thus linked himself to it directly, which is why, when the ring is eventually destroyed in The Return of the King, Sauron's body is permanently vanquished, and his spirit becomes a shadow over Middle-earth, one effortlessly blown away (no, he's not a giant flaming eye). We may be a long way off from that, but The Rings of Power has set the stage.

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 is available for streaming on Prime Video, with Season 4 premiering on a date yet to be unveiled.

Chris Pratt's new movie, Way of the Warrior Kid, isn't exactly winning over critics.

Industry observers note that the Guardians of the Galaxy star has had a busy year, reprising Mario in the latest Super Mario sequel and Lt. Commander James Reece in The Terminal List season 2. Recent findings suggest that with 13 reviews, Way of the Warrior Kid debuted to an underwhelming 31% on Rotten Tomatoes. More importantly, he ends his busy year on a lukewarm note, as all three of his movie releases recorded below 60%. His sci-fi movie, Mercy, tallied 24%, while the Nintendo sequel, The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, earned 42%. Lastly, it extends a poor streak, as critics did not receive his five movies well. The Super Mario Galaxy Movie (2026).

According to recent reports, critics found many concerns with the adaptation, particularly its heavy emphasis on a military tone over the coming-of-age underdog story, its over-the-top third act, and its thinly written narrative. Some reviews also saw that the movie was overly formulaic and melodramatic. Meanwhile, some positive aspects include the message and strong dynamic between Pratt and Hill.

Industry observers note that in ScreenRant's review of Way of the Warrior Kid, Alex Harrison sums up that the adaptation "is sleek to the point of becoming simplistic" and "it's too frictionless an experience." The assessment also notes that the movie "gives it a propagandistic quality," a point other critics had argued. Meanwhile, Pratt's performance doesn't always land beyond his comedy timing, as his portrayal is "fairly sleepy." Nevertheless, Way of the Warrior Kid earned a 5 out of 10 stars, with the finale being the saving grace.

Sources indicate that although critical reception has been polarizing, Pratt's movie may still win over audiences, especially given its underdog premise and familiar themes. In fact, his last few movies earned positive viewer responses, so it's entirely possible the same could happen with Way of the Warrior Kid. It's unclear whether there are plans to adapt the remaining books, but that will ultimately come down to the movie's viewership numbers on Apple TV.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, Pratt remains a very busy actor and producer. He will partner with Paramount to adapt the sci-fi drama The Traveler and will eventually reprise Star-Lord/Peter Quill in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, though it's unclear whether he will appear in Avengers: Doomsday or Secret Wars. He's also dedicated to the Terminal List universe after teasing a narrative shift with season 3.

McG, who helmed Terminator Salvation and This Means War, directed the adaptation, while Will Staples penned the screenplay. Linda Cardelinni, Levi McConaughey, Ava Torres, Darien Sills-Evans, and Carl McDowell round out the supporting cast. Pratt is one of the producers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, spoilers are never late, nor are they early, but arrive precisely when they mean to. This article discusses major plot details from the Season 3 finale of "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power.".

According to recent reports, sometimes, in the darkest moments life has to offer us, all we need is a friend. Throughout the most recent episodes of "The Rings of Power" Season 3, the gentle wizard Gandalf (Daniel Weyman) has struggled to temper his hasty inclinations and listen to what fate has in store for him in combatting the rise of Sauron's (Charlie Vickers) evil in Middle-earth. The solution? Repeatedly, he's told that his purpose isn't to fight and defeat evil, whether it be the Dark Lord himself or simply the Dark Wizard known as Pallando (Ciarán Hinds). Instead, he's to save those seduced by the darkness — or, as he eloquently puts it in the finale, "to inspire good" in others.

Sources indicate that he learned that lesson in the first two seasons of "The Rings of Power," in fact, thanks to one diminutive friend and ally: the Harfoot Elanor "Nori" Brandyfoot (Markella Kavenagh). Unfortunately, these proto-Hobbits have been missing in action throughout Season 3, but that finally changes once Gandalf finds himself imprisoned in Mordor. After rebuffing Sauron's offer of one of his remaining rings of power, the wizard suddenly wakes up inside a cell with Nori at his side, claiming to have been there for weeks. Obviously, this is yet another of Sauron's deceptions, and Gandalf rapidly sees through the façade.

Still, it's undeniably nostalgic to see Nori back again and playing a significant role in a story that seemed to have moved beyond her. Thankfully, this cameo isn't the last we see of her, either. Her next appearance is the episode's best, most poignant moment.

From horror to heartbreak to happiness, viewers were taken for quite an emotional ride in the Season 3 finale of "The Rings of Power." Nori's first appearance in that cell with Gandalf likely caught many by surprise, even if it seemed to be too good (or, in these circumstances, too bad) to be true. It surely strains credulity to imagine that Sauron's forces somehow tracked down one random Harfoot somewhere in the wilds of Middle-earth, hauled her back to Mordor, and kept her around just in case Gandalf ever came knocking ... and, thankfully, showrunners/writers J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay don't beat around the bush for long.

Industry observers note that but it's what happens next that puts a fitting bow on her return. After Gandalf escapes his cell and attempts to win Pallando back to the side of the heroes, we're treated to a montage sequence taking us all across Middle-earth. We see Galadriel (Morfydd Clark) and Celeborn (Jamie Campbell Bower) walking hand in hand, the prideful King Pharazôn (Trystan Gravelle) on the eve of battle, and, finally, the real Nori sitting by a campfire looking up at the moon and likely thinking of her old pal Gandalf.

Industry observers note that there's no way to say whether "The Rings of Power" will make room for the Harfoots again in the upcoming fourth season, but we can certainly hope! Their lovably rustic (but tenderhearted) dynamic, embodied through Nori's yearning for adventure and her innate sense of right and wrong, lent plenty of gravitas to Gandalf's early journeying. The finale's acknowledgement of that bond speaks volumes, and it makes us hope we haven't seen the last of her, Poppy (Megan Richards), and the rest of their Harfoot clan.

In a recent development, in the lead-up to the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, Sony and Rockstar Games have stated that the highly anticipated game "plays best on PS5." For some gamers looking to purchase a console solely to play GTA 6​​​​​​​, this statement may be the deciding factor in getting an Xbox or a PlayStation. Yet, about a week after the game was released, it now appears that Xbox gamers may not actually be at as great a disadvantage​​​​​​​ as Sony would like you to think.

In a recent development, the tech aficionados at Digital Foundry have published a comprehensive comparison of how GTA 6 runs on all available platforms. While the details of the report are fascinating, let's cut right to the shocking results. It turns out GTA 6 actually plays better on Xbox... in the right circumstances. When comparing the base PlayStation 5 to the Xbox Series X (which are relatively equivalent), Digital Foundry discovered that while the visuals are basically the same on the two consoles, there is a clearer distinction when comparing performance​​​​​​​. Digital Foundry stated that "PS5 suffers substantially more frequent frame-rate drops than Series X, which is compounded by the fact that the Xbox machine also benefits from 120 Hz VRR support to smooth out minor dips," concluding that "Ultimately​​​​​​​, Series X is meaningfully better off.".

According to recent reports, it is crucial to note that Digital Foundry's study is strictly focused on technical performance, which ignores a big reason GTA 6 has been stated to play best on PS5: the controller. Sony's DualSense offers unique features like haptic feedback and adaptive triggers tuned to every little detail in the game, such as the weight of a gas pedal in a car or the buzz of a phone. It makes the experience more immersive.​​​​​​​ To the average gamer, the slight difference between Xbox Series X and PS5 may not be as noticeable as the difference the DualSense makes.​​​​​​​ But tech heads will be glad to know this.​​​​​​​.

Even with the surprise that Xbox Series X plays somewhat better than the base PS5, Digital Foundry still asserts that PS5 Pro ​​​​​​​delivers the definitive GTA 6 experience​​​​​​​ thanks to its larger GPU, Sony's PSSR upscaling, and more. All of this allows for the most stable version of GTA 6. Given the price​​​​​​​ of every console on the market right now, individual gamers will have to decide whether the technical benefits justify the ever-growing cost of hardware​​​​​​​.

Sources indicate that xbox gets another win with the budget Xbox Series S. ​​​​​​​Despite being significantly less powerful than every other Xbox and PlayStation console on which GTA 6 is available​​​​​​​, the Series S still manages to put up a good fight. This is accomplished by lowering visual quality​​​​​​​ and taking advantage of upscaling from 720p to 1080p. While less stable than the Series X, Digital Foundry noted that the image quality is still decent.

#120853. Industry News: Movie Theaters in 2026: Filmmakers and Exhibitors on What’s Good, What’s Bad, and What’s Changing
