💡 Key Takeaways
  • [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on October 27, 2026 during the 2026 AFI Film Festival.
  • There have been any number of movies about the hell of fighting in World War II, the most visceral of which have been made in the years since “Saving Private Ryan” provided a very enduring template for how modern filmmakers could render that carnage with both the spectacle of a blockbuster and the horror of a memory.
  • According to recent reports, what differentiates this unsparing epic from the scores of other stories about the Greatest Generation, however, is that some of its characters are good at football.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

[Editor’s note: This review was originally published on October 27, 2026 during the 2026 AFI Film Festival. The film is available to stream on Netflix today.].

There have been any number of movies about the hell of fighting in World War II, the most visceral of which have been made in the years since “Saving Private Ryan” provided a very enduring template for how modern filmmakers could render that carnage with both the spectacle of a blockbuster and the horror of a memory. Peter Berg’s brutal and concussive “The Mosquito Bowl” is definitely one of them! No one could ever say that it’s not.

According to recent reports, what differentiates this unsparing epic from the scores of other stories about the Greatest Generation, however, is that some of its characters are good at football. Indeed, these All-American college boys are so good at football that, on Christmas Eve 1944, the soldiers are ordered to play a morale-boosting game of two-hand touch on the beach where their units are preparing for the Battle of Okinawa. Related Stories Lauren Ambrose on Playing the Mother of a Missing Teen in ‘The Unbelievers’ and Why ‘Six Feet Under’ Is a Hit with Gen Z ‘Paper Tiger’: James Gray Convinced Adam Driver He Was Playing the Hero, Then Crafted His Mythic End.

According to recent reports, and for the span of the eight-minute montage during which “The Mosquito Bowl” actually makes good on its title, it’s easy to picture how the famous scrimmage — fought between a roster of impossibly beautiful athletes in their primes — might have been used to backstop a story that accentuated the senseless waste of sending thousands of young men to their deaths. Alas, for the rest of this 126-minute film, that waste is better expressed through Berg’s failure to make anything more of their lives, as the “Spenser Confidential” auteur’s latest Netflix project does almost nothing else to distinguish itself from a genre so well-worn that it’s seemingly run out of ways to blow up a human body.

Recent findings suggest that why “almost”? I was hoping you wouldn’t ask. For starters, there’s the decision to cast thin-skinned ESPN commentator Pat McAfee as an R. Lee Ermey-inspired drill sergeant. “The Mosquito Bowl” also stands out for how confusingly it conflates the thrill and teamwork of combat sport with the violence and camaraderie of armed conflict; war is presented as both a natural extension of what these boys have been trained to do on the gridiron (to the point that the soldiers briefly diagram their initiative of attack as if it were a football play), and also the catastrophe that robbed them of a more innocent purpose. (Berg loves the troops as much as he hates the fact that generals and presidents so wantonly sacrifice their lives.) Someone declares that “The Marine Corps is the greatest offensive line in history,” and yet the film’s characters don’t seem to have any special advantages on the field of battle, as it would be glib to suggest that even the country’s best college running back might be able to slip free of a mortar blast. It’s one thing to argue that football is war, and another, much more asinine thing to argue that war is football.

Perhaps that’s why the Mosquito Bowl itself only took up a single page of the Buzz Bissinger book on which Berg’s film is based, and why that source material used the game as a lens through which a light could be shined on the semi-forgotten men who found their way into the lineup that day. It’s been suggested that Bissinger played up the sports angle in order to capitalize on the success of his “Friday Night Lights,” and given that Berg adapted that book into a film as well, it stands to reason that his “Mosquito Bowl” should do the same.

The problem is that, in stark contrast to Bissinger, Berg and co-writer Mark L. Smith only seem to care about their characters as a means to an end. The project’s anti-war ethos is solely conveyed by reducing collegiate legends into cannon fodder, as the movie is considerably less interested in what bonds these boys together than it is in the shells that blast them apart.

Perhaps that explains why I’ve been able to write almost 650 words without bothering to mention any of their names. To the extent that it matters to a film so blandly de-saturated that everyone in it looks half-dead from the start, Nicholas Galitzine stars as Brown University legend John McLaughry — the only character we know for certain will survive the assault on Japan. (The movie opens with a sustained flash-forward of John staring longingly at an empty football field as “Friday Night Lights” veterans Explosions in the Sky layer their post-rock shimmer over the soundtrack). He’s got sad eyes, a square jaw, and a brunette girlfriend, which is more than you can say for Bob Baumann (Bill Skarsgård), who has a devil-may-care attitude that disappears real quick once his unit makes land on Tawara. The only real source of contextual friction is owed to the rivalry between Purdue fullback Tony Butkovich (a glinty and magnetic Ray Nicholson) and the straight-laced mama’s boy he beat in a substantial game before the attack on Pearl Harbor (Tom Francis as the stoic and decent Dave Schreiner).

Sources indicate that individually, Butkovich is the only one of these characters who has the chutzpah to carry the movie on his back. Incidentally, he’s the only one of these men who was heading to the pros before the war got in the way. Still, it’s engaging to see them all blitz through life on their home turf, and “The Mosquito Bowl” benefits from Berg’s handheld and ruggedly naturalistic approach to how the players comport themselves off the field (read: they say “fuck” a lot and generally aspire to feel more like real people than they do patronizing impressions of what men were like in the ’40s).

Recent findings suggest that but then the war comes to Hawaii, a match-cut turns a flock of birds into some fighter jets, and these beloved football stars all find themselves rendered nearly anonymous by the sea of shaved heads that are waiting for them at book. Little is made of their civilian celebrity, and even less of their individual decisions to enlist. “This is my rifle — there are many others like it, but this one is mine.”.

Recent findings suggest that berg takes militaristic uniformity as all the excuse he needs to avoid deviating from expectation, and nearly everything that happens between basic training and the big game on the beach near Okinawa feels like it could have happened in several dozen other World War II movies, and almost certainly did. Defiant warriors curdle into terrified kids, bullets whizz through ocean waves, snipers pick off predictable characters at unsuspecting — or very suspecting — moments, and even the most hardened of marines find themselves staring blankly into the middle distance as their friends are decimated on all sides. Berg has always had a flair for the frenetic, and while there’s a perversely fetishistic veneer to the attention he devotes to entrails and enemy screams, it serves the film’s purposes that war has seldom seemed less survivable than it does here. (The film has no interest in humanizing the Japanese, but tries to compensate for that by presenting a few of the Americans as unrepentant monsters).

Industry observers note that still, for all of its supposed verisimilitude, “The Mosquito Bowl” seems less indebted to the reality of war than it does to Hollywood’s idea of it, and its abject refusal to flesh out its characters — a dereliction of duty, if ever there was one — makes it feel more contrived rather than less. I’m happy for Berg that he found a way to combine all of his favorite things into a single project (football, the military, and massive fireballs are all well-accounted for, even if Mark Wahlberg’s absence makes the whole movie feel like it’s forgotten something crucial), but “The Mosquito Bowl” accomplishes very little beyond violently illustrating that war is worse than football. It does that with such fervor that it loses all sight of what those things might really have in common.

In a recent development, netflix will release “The Mosquito Bowl” in theaters on Friday, October 30. It will be available to stream on Netflix starting Wednesday, November 25.

In one of Doomsday's trailers, Reed screams at Victor, questioning if he is responsible for what has happened. It's clear that the two have crossed paths previously, even if the MCU hasn't shown that.

According to Pascal, Doom and Richards are "bonded in a lot of different ways." As he told Empire, this is rooted in their scientific and mathematical minds. They have an extensive relationship in the comics, going back to their days as college roommates. While it's unknown if that is part of RDJ's Doom's backstory, Pascal teased that the friendship they share makes them "feel less alone in the world.".

Sources indicate that considering Reed's history with Doom, it is hardly a surprise that Sue Storm (Vanessa Kirby) also interacted with him previously. While Reed and Victor may have bonded over science, Sue seems to have a better grasp on who he really was.

It has been revealed that her relationship with Doom is strong enough that she's the one who explains to the film's other characters how he used to be. A special look at Doomsday began with Sue telling her new allies, "Victor was always the smartest guy in every room. He used to be different. He used to be kind. He used to be caring.   • Recent findings suggest that I don't know anyone who wouldn't appreciate finding these display glasses in their Christmas stocking.
  • It can be hard to buy a gift for a health-focused person.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that our grandparents could drop some treats in a sock and call it Christmas, secure in the knowledge that their children would be delighted by an orange. These days, though, everyone from your tech-obsessed granny to your cutting-edge teen wants to be impressed. Luckily, there's a mind-blowing high-tech gadget out there for everyone.

Recent findings suggest that I don't know anyone who wouldn't appreciate finding these display glasses in their Christmas stocking. The Xbx a01s are sunglasses you can plug into any device with a USB-C port to create your own personal, private monitor. The resulting picture is the equivalent of a 142" TV. The refresh rate is a crisp 120Hz, and the glasses support HDR10 and real-time SDR-to-HDR upscaling and billions of colors, all in a package that weighs only 62 grams. In other words: It's an HD TV you can carry in your pocket and wear on your face. The $299 list price won't break your wallet either. They're the best smart glasses for most people. Check out my full review for more details.

It can be hard to buy a gift for a health-focused person. They usually don't want booze and they like putting in effort. But the Whoop Peak 5 fitness tracker will brighten the Christmas morning of the most diehard athlete. It's more versatile than a watch (you can wear it on your bicep and even in your underwear) and it monitors heart rate, respiratory rate, heart rate variability, skin temperature, blood oxygen levels, daily activity, and sleep—basically everything I don't worry about. Check out Lifehacker's senior health editor Beth Skwarecki's in-depth look at the Whoop Peak 5 for more details.

You cannot go wrong with a GoPro. The tech giant's easy-to-use, hard-to-break cameras are synonymous with "action photography" and compact enough to fit in a stocking. If there's a snowboarder, skateboarder, kayaker, or BMX racer on your list, this is a must. Even if your giftee isn't an adventurer, the GoPro Hero 13 supports additional lenses and filters that let customers go beyond the "gnarly fish-eye, dude" photography and videography of past generations. Check out associate tech editor Michelle Ehrhardt's GoPro Hero 13 review for more details.

Everyone wants their own droid. Beni from Mondo Robotics is a camera robot that takes 4K video while autonomously following its subject wherever they go. If you want to get action footage, there's no need to hassle with a tripod or another person: You can control Beni with the remote, or simply tell it to follow you. It can be set to track you from behind, from the side, or it can circle you, and you can adjust what it is doing from the app or remote on the fly, so there's no limit to the kind of elaborate shots it can pull off. Plus it's freakin' adorable. The $799 list price might be a bit steep for most gift-givers, but as far as how well it works and how much fun I've had using it, it's worth the money.

The R36 Max 2 retro handheld game console lets you take your gaming anywhere. It comes with over 20,000 games pre-installed, so you can play every title from classic consoles like the Atari 2600 or the PlayStation 1, as well as just about every arcade game anyone ever dropped a coin into, all for less than $100. I paid more than that in quarters just to beat Dragon's Lair!

It has been revealed that I'm obsessed with the Yamaha Seqtrak. It crams a drum machine, sequencer, sampler, three separate synthesizers, and a speaker into a package small enough to put into a Christmas stocking. It's a complete mobile studio—everything you need to produce a song or beat—but it also integrates with your computer's DAW and other MIDI gear to become part of your home studio. All that for only $300!

Recent findings suggest that the Flipper Zero is a must-have device for the hardcore, glasses-wearing, circuit-bender type of techie. Its ability to do evil deeds like hack ATMs is greatly exaggerated, but the Flipper is still a technological Swiss Army knife that lets you read and manipulate the invisible waves around you, from radio waves to RFID, NFC, Bluetooth, and wifi signals. It's educational, fascinating, and powerful; how you use that power is your business.

If you're giving a gift to a would-be Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, this miniature, wireless microscope will rock their holiday. It's easy to set up, works with PCs, Android, or iOS devices, magnifies things up to 1000x, and takes 1080p pictures of your discoveries.

Ray Bradbury’s 'Fahrenheit 451' Officially Returns in 2027

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (320 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stories like Ray Bradbury's 1953 novel Fahrenheit 451 have remained timely throughout the years.
  • Sources indicate that the upcoming images show imagery of the burning of books that became so connected to Bradbury's work.
  • Fahrenheit 451 has been adapted multiple times, with the most recent adaptation coming in 2018 from Ramin Bahrani, starring Michael B.

Stories like Ray Bradbury's 1953 novel Fahrenheit 451 have remained timely throughout the years. Written as a critique of censorship and the act of book burning, the novel has been adapted into many different formats, and now a new take on it is heading our way through a new graphic novel from artist Victor Santos. Collider is thrilled to announce that Titan Comics' new graphic novel has the approval of the Bradbury estate and will be released in July 2027. To celebrate the new release of Fahrenheit 451, Collider is thrilled to bring you an exclusive new look at the artwork from Santos' stunning adaptation of Bradbury's timeless work.

Sources indicate that the upcoming images show imagery of the burning of books that became so connected to Bradbury's work. From ripped pages falling to the books themselves sitting in an ashy pile, the work that Santos is doing in his adaptation is truly something remarkable. Santos is an Eisner and Harvey Award-winning artist and has been the co-creator of such graphic novels as Filthy Rich, Rashomon, Bad Girls, Against Hope, and Violent Love.

Fahrenheit 451 has been adapted multiple times, with the most recent adaptation coming in 2018 from Ramin Bahrani, starring Michael B. Jordan as Guy Montag and Sofia Boutella as Clarisse. But the story, as a whole, is still timely in a way that even back in the 1950s, people couldn't have predicted. Bradbury's original work was looking at the way that television can inform and manipulate stories, influencing people who are not willing to read and do the research themselves. That is still just as topical today, and using a graphic novel to share that story adds a whole new layer to the narrative.

It has been revealed that you can get your copy of Fahrenheit 451 in July of next year for $24.99 from Titan Comics. Stay tuned at Collider for more.

Industry News: 10 Hacks Every 'GTA 6' Player Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1241 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, I've been playing Grand Theft Auto VI since launch, and I'm having a blast so far.
  • Industry observers note that I'm not going to share any spoilers here, but you should know that the side quests in Chapter 1 are vital.
  • If you're used to playing racing games, you'll find the driving experience in GTA VI to be quite different.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I've been playing Grand Theft Auto VI since launch, and I'm having a blast so far. The world feels even more detailed and immersive than previous GTA games, which means there's a lot to learn beyond the basic tutorials and prompts the game shares at the beginning. These are the 10 GTA 6 hacks I used to improve the game's quality of life. If you do the same, you'll spend more time immersed in the world, and less time fighting the game's default settings.

Industry observers note that I'm not going to share any spoilers here, but you should know that the side quests in Chapter 1 are vital. If you ignore all the optional quests or small asks by other characters, you won't be able to return to those later. These are small things like fixing up the house for Lucia, meditating with her, and buying her a necklace when she asks you to. All of these have an impact on your progress. Take your time in this chapter, and remember to save before starting the mission called "Recalibration." That mission leads to Tourist Trap, which is the point of no return for Chapter 1.

If you're used to playing racing games, you'll find the driving experience in GTA VI to be quite different. It's hard to keep an eye on minimap directions while you're also getting used to vehicles in the game, and I used voice navigation to ensure that I don't keep getting lost, particularly for time-sensitive missions. You can enable this by going to GTA VI settings > Audio > GPS Voice > Voice. If you're playing the game on PS5, your DualSense controller's speaker plays GPS voice prompts. This is great as those alerts can be hard to hear over all other in-game sounds from your TV's speaker.

Using GTA 6's default controls, making Jason and Lucia run is quite annoying. The game makes you hold L3 to run, which hurts my thumbs. If you alter movement speed in settings, you can make the characters run just by using the left stick. You can walk by easing off the left stick, or switch to a fast walk, jog, or run when you push the stick all the way. Tweak this by going to GTA VI settings > Gameplay > Movement Speed > Jog. This lets you move faster without draining your stamina. You can also change from Jog to Run if you want the fastest possible movement speed with the left stick. Having noted that, my pro tip is to go to Control Scheme in settings, and switch to Classic. This lets you run by holding the X button, as opposed to L3 with default controls.

Haptic strength is one area where GTA 6 takes the immersion a bit too far, as it's dialed up to the maximum level by default. This makes the controller's vibration strength a bit too intense for my liking, and also has a negative impact on battery life. You can fix that by reducing haptic strength a little. It's under GTA VI settings > Controller > Vibration & Haptics Strength.

Many modern controllers develop "stick drift," an issue where small movements of the analog sticks register as large inputs. This causes a massive problem in games that require precise inputs, such as GTA 6. To counter this potential problem, the game allows you to adjust the deadzone for each analog stick in your controller. That mentioned, this setting can be used to your advantage, even if you don't have stick drift issues in your controller. I recommend dialing up the deadzone to 7 to improve the driving experience. I find most cars in GTA 6 to be a bit floaty to drive, and adjusting the deadzone fixes this issue to a large extent.

Committing a heist attracts heat in GTA 6, and there are many different ways to escape the attention of in-game cops. The usual tricks include stocking up on outfits to change into, parking your vehicle a block or two away, and being so stealthy that you leave no witnesses to your crimes. However, an underrated trick involves using the pickup truck you get at the start of the game. Get a bike in the game, and stash it in your pickup truck. Then, use the truck to drive to the crime scene, and hide the truck a short distance away. Unload the bike, and use it to get to the crime scene. Once the heist is complete, ditch the bike, and run to your truck. Witnesses won't have seen you using the truck, which allows you to escape the area rapidly.

According to recent reports, if you are using a car as a getaway vehicle, you can use two tricks to make a smooth escape. First, double-tap the Triangle button to exit your vehicle without switching off its engine. When you return to the vehicle in a hurry, you can escape a lot faster. If you have quick fingers, you can double-tap Triangle first, and just as your character is about to exit the vehicle, press L3 (or X, if you use classic controls). This leaves the car's door open, and saves you a little more time when you're fleeing.

I suffer from chronic migraines, and I am sensitive to bright lights. Fortunately, GTA 6 has a bunch of accessibility settings that help me play the game for longer. Even if you don't face the same problems, these settings will help reduce eye strain in longer play sessions. Go to GTA VI settings > Display > Flashbang, and switch to Dark. This stops flashbangs from showing a bright white light when they go off. On the same settings page, you can tweak Player Status Effects Intensity to reduce screen effects when your character is low on health or stamina. You can also enable Brightness Reduction to reduce the intensity of bright lights in the game, and try Focus Trail Colorblind Mode if you find it hard to distinguish between different colors.

I haven't been able to play first-person shooters for decades because the camera movement makes me nauseous and gives me a headache. Of late, I've noticed that it's getting harder to play third-person games too. My first two hours in GTA 6 had me quite worried because I was feeling quite sick, and I had to turn off my PS5. Luckily for me, I found a few tweaks to mitigate this problem. You can do that in GTA VI settings > UI > Persistent Center Dot. This permanently shows a white dot in the center of the screen, and it reduced my motion sickness enough to help me play the game. You can also go to GTA VI settings > Camera, reduce Camera Bob, and turn off Camera Shake, and Weapon Sway. I also recommend going to the Controller tab in settings, and tweaking all the options under Aim & Look Sensitivity until you find a comfortable level.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 includes realistic ringing sounds that linger after explosions in the game. This may be fine for some people, but it can negatively affect some players' gaming sessions. Those who suffer from tinnitus or chronic migraines may not enjoy those ringing sounds, and, luckily, the game allows you to disable them. Open GTA 6's in-game settings, and enable the feature from Audio > Tinnitus Reduction.

Breaking: 8 Highlights That Fell Off Hard After Season 1

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1641 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Even the most popular TV series have experienced dips in quality, and even highlights whose premieres made some of the splashiest entrances in television history have struggled to maintain their intrigue through to the finish line.
  • It has been revealed that lost, the 2004 ABC phenomenon that dominated water cooler conversation for years, boasts one of the most controversial series finales of all time.
  • In a recent development, similarly, mid-series stumbles are also frequent, even among shows that managed to stick the landing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even the most popular TV series have experienced dips in quality, and even highlights whose premieres made some of the splashiest entrances in television history have struggled to maintain their intrigue through to the finish line. Of course, shows that are strong from start to finish are the gold standard of TV writing, but, unfortunately, controversial or disappointing finales are far more common.

It has been revealed that lost, the 2004 ABC phenomenon that dominated water cooler conversation for years, boasts one of the most controversial series finales of all time. More recently, Jason Bateman's critically acclaimed Ozark had a notoriously lackluster ending that seemed to have largely brought mainstream discussion of the show to a close in tandem with its story.

In a recent development, similarly, mid-series stumbles are also frequent, even among shows that managed to stick the landing. The beloved Friday Night Lights has a now-infamous second season, while House, despite its widely appreciated ending, struggled through the immediate aftermath of a major character exit.

Sources indicate that crucially, though, these hits found their way back to solid storytelling. The same can't be remarked for these indicates that lost their way after their first season and never recovered.

In its first season, Heroes felt like an excitingly original take on the superhero genre. The story, about a group of average individuals who belatedly discover they have world-saving abilities, was grounded, earnest, and exciting. The high stakes of a genuine world-ending event kept the story focused and the energy up, while still leaving room for down-to-earth character development.

The looming threat of an explosion and the clear implications of what would follow drove the plot of Heroes season 1. Season 2, though, didn't share season 1's urgency. The season pivoted its focus to the potential outbreak of an ominous virus, but the show didn't actually introduce the virus' apocalyptic potential until episode 7.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, the other aspects of the series were similarly weak compared to the tight intrigue of season 1. Series creator Tim Kring himself admitted that Heroes season 2 suffered from slow plot progression, detached character development, and stilted romantic arcs that didn't suit the show. Seasons 3 and 4 unfortunately continued Heroes' transition from earnest and exciting to serious and heavy-handed.

In a recent development, 13 Reasons Why, the emotionally mature young adult novel by Jay Asher, took the world by storm when it came out in 2007. Ten years later, Netflix's adaptation had a similar impact. The show's first season embraced the novel's unflinching treatment of the topics of suicide and sexual assault, respecting its young audience enough to tell such a raw, emotional story. The audience appreciated the gesture.

In a recent development, season 2, however, continued on where the source material concluded, and a tone that was once mature and raw had become graphic and shocking. The story's premise was already dark enough to stop viewers in their tracks, yet each subsequent season of 13 Reasons Why seemed to be trying to one-up itself, making the show increasingly contrived and seemingly upsetting viewers just for the sake of it.

In a recent development, this was a trend that began in season 2 and persisted through to the end. 13 Reasons Why season 3 earned an 11% on Rotten Tomatoes compared to season 1's 77%. By the time it reached the end, it wasn't a stretch to argue that 13 Reasons Why was Netflix's most controversial show of all time.

Broadchurch's first outing remains a standout in the now-saturated small town murder mystery genre. Co-leads David Tennant and Olivia Colman gave, arguably, career-best performances as the show explored a tight-knit community's descent into grief and suspicion.

Industry observers note that throughout season 1, Broadchurch excelled at not only solving the mystery of 11-year-old Danny Latimer's death, but also at exploring the psychological impact the event had on the ecosystem of the town as a whole. In a unique move for the murder mystery format, Broadchurch seasons 2 and 3 largely continued to explore the fallout of Danny's death rather than fully pivoting to a latest mystery.

In a recent development, while new characters and stories were introduced, the show also preserved its focus on the Latimers, attempting a truly in-depth psychological exploration of the tragedy. With the case closed, though, Broadchurch's subsequent seasons suffered for feeling more like they were belaboring the point and overstaying their welcome than they were breaking new ground.

Westworld season 1 is still considered some of HBO's best work. Yet the rest of the series has proven to be such a disappointment that HBO Max no longer even has the show available to stream.

Industry observers note that westworld came when variations on the neo-Western genre were in full swing, and there has still not been anything that captures the eerie, desolate, futuristic cowboy atmosphere like HBO's quietly star-studded series. Aaron Paul, James Marsden, Jeffrey Wright, Ed Harris, Anthony Hopkins, Evan Rachel Wood, and Luke Hemsworth all starred in a series whose greatness was quickly cut short.

After its excellent first season, Westworld's plot grew both increasingly convoluted and increasingly removed from the Western setting that made it so visually unique. Creators Jonathan Nolan and Lisa Gilroy have since moved on to executive producing Fallout, another retrofuturistic show that encapsulates a Western energy, so far with more enduring success than Westworld.

Like Westworld, True Detective is an HBO series famous for a first season so impressive that the show's future installments were unable to follow in its own footsteps. Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson delivered what were undoubtedly career-best performances in the Southern Gothic crime series, while the story's exploration of themes of masculinity and degrees of evil made the season truly poetic.

It has been revealed that in this case, the show's anthology format didn't work in its favor, as the next season had to maintain the quality of the first without any of the actors, stories, or settings that had so endeared audiences to the show. Every latest cast and new mystery True Detective has tried so far has failed to live up to the expectation set by season 1, but the anthology format does give each new season a fresh opportunity to try.

In fact, True Detective's upcoming fifth season might be the most promising yet, as the show has recently made the buzzy announcement that Nicolas Cage and Antonio Banderas will star as the season's leading detectives.

Hulu almost certainly hoped that Nine Perfect Strangers would become its own Big Little Lies​​​​. Similarly based on an excellent and popular Liane Moriarty novel, the cast of Nine Perfect Strangers season 1 conveyed the show's confidence. Melissa McCarthy, Bobby Cannavale, and Manny Jacinto rounded out the group of guests and staff at the wellness retreat run by Nicole Kidman's Masha Dmitrichenko.

According to recent reports, though it never quite reached the height of the novel's quality, Nine Perfect Strangers season 1 was a perfectly enjoyable retelling of the story that delivered on the promise of bringing the eccentric resort to life. Season 2, though, went out of its way to continue the story where the novel concluded, bringing a latest set of strangers into Masha's latest experimental wellness endeavor.

Despite the addition of the likes of Annie Murphy, Henry Golding, and Christine Baranski, the characters of Nine Perfect Strangers season 2 felt empty, while the plot felt both convoluted and aimless. The season sacrificed the intrigue of the connection of strangers in favor of revealing Masha's contrived and melodramatic backstory. The fate of Nine Perfect Strangers season 3 is still up in the air.

Beef is the latest in the increasing trend of limited series rebranding themselves as ongoing anthology series in the wake of the first season's success. Netflix's surprisingly earnest and surreal saga between Steven Yeun's Danny and Ali Wong's Amy quickly became what was arguably one of the streamer's highest-quality original productions.

The plot, which began with a minor road rage incident and quickly spiraled out of control, was unexpected at every turn, ultimately offering perceptive observations of Asian-American culture, conflict, and individuality. The season wrapped up in a satisfying conclusion that left no aspect of the story untold. The strong conclusion led to the announcement of Beef season 2 being met with both excitement and wariness.

Industry observers note that both proved to be valid emotions, as the ensemble cast of Oscar Isaac, Carey Mulligan, Charles Melton, and Cailee Spaeny all delivered impressive performances. Nonetheless, the plot felt more like an aspirational season of The White Lotus than something on par with the truly creative Beef season 1.

Sources indicate that the Following began as one of the most exciting network TV outings of the 2010s. James Purefoy and Kevin Bacon starred in The Following's cat-and-mouse game between a former FBI agent and a murderous, Edgar Allan Poe-obsessed cult leader. Purefoy's charisma and the eerily strange nature of his crimes made the show stand out within the tried-and-true crime drama genre.

Like many highlights that dropped off in quality early on, season 1 ended naturally with a climactic event that seemed to resolve the central conflict on both a plot and character level. The show's popularity, though, led to a season 2 renewal that forced The Following to walk back its powerful season 1 finale and manufacture a reason to keep Purefoy's Joe Carroll in the fray.

Industry observers note that as the series earned not just a second but a third season, Joe Carroll's continued existence began to stretch the limits of believability, as did the reach of his cult, which seemed capable of thwarting Bacon's Ryan Hardy at every possible turn. Like several of these series, The Following would have a very different legacy had it ended on a high note after season 1.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot at the moment “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

Recent findings suggest that “We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

According to recent reports, “We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz.

Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw.

At that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

It has been revealed that cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

According to recent reports, liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré. Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88).

They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

Yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

Diligent defensive work by Ngumoha stops Konate’s run down the outside left.

A final substitution, hopefully. Brunner replaces Biereth. Konate’s shot, a pearoller, is easily saved by Mamardashvili after A mix-up between Kerkez and Munoz.

As usual, the substitutions have killed the game. Watched Leeds vs RB Leipzig yesterday. They played two 60 minute matches which kept it more competitive for longer but still descended into a kickabout late on.

Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

According to recent reports, monaco also made changes, four I think. Will catch up with then once they’re confirmed. Ramsey is into the game straight away tp stop Coulibaly’s shot.

Ramsay, Chiesa and Elliott are coming on for Szoboszlai, Frimpong and Koumas. Lovely applause for Elliott.

Industry observers note that konate sweeps a left-foot shot from the left of the box past the right post with Mamardashvili forced into a headlong dive. Liverpool have lost their defensive shape and intensity, allowing Monaco to punch holes through the lines with some direct running.

Nazinho gets round Frimpong down the Monaco left and cuts back the perfect pass to put it on a plate for Coulibaly who hammers a left-foot shot from the right of the D that Mamardashvili throws up his hands to block. That would have stung. Good save. A flag would have meant it wouldn’t have counted but even so Frimpong’s defensive work wasn’t good enough.

Recent findings suggest that it’s been very scrappy since the changes but then Ngumoha pounces on to a loose ball, glides up the right and tries to play Koumas in behind the back four. Sadly, he overhits the pass which trickles out for a goal-kick. Cue an ovation and cries of ‘Rio! Rio!’.

Three changes for Monaco with Detoubet, Abline and Camara departing for Benzhara, Coulibaly and Konaté.

Ngumoha has gone to the right wing and Koumas is playing through the middle as a false nine.

Liverpool make five changes with Gakpo, Van Dijk, Wirtz, Tsimikas and Isak departing while Munoz makes his ‘debut’ with Ngumoha, Nyoni, Chambers, McConell and Kerkez.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 2 (Biereth) Mistake by Gravenberch allows Golovin to play a pass into the left half of the box for Biereth. His first shot is well saved by Mamardashvili at full stretch but his tenacity allowed him to get to the rebound ahead of Endo, swivel and stick his second effort in to equalise.

In a recent development, monaco overplay at the edge of the box, Detourbet, Biereth and Abline playing ‘after you. Claud’, instead of shooting.

A slick, short passing move between Gravenberch, Wirtz and Isak ends with Isak on the deck in the box after Gravenberch’s step-over allowed the ball to run to him. Isak took a touch to move the ball on to his left but gave the defender a glimmer of it and he hacked it away before felling Isak as well as collateral damage.

Quiet start to the half. Biereth just pressed Mamardashvili but the keeper managed to sweep the ball away even though under more pressure than he would have expected.

Liverpool try to play out from the back with Mamardashvili spearing a straight pass to Gravenberch who tried to knock it round the corner for Endo but the ball skidded under his studs and out for a throw-in.

It has been revealed that isak is apparently claiming both goals. Replays are indistinct. He could have clipped it in off his heel as he had a swing at the ball while grounded at the same time as Wirtz.

Endo has slotted in at centre-back alongside Van Dijk.

Half-time changes: Mamardashvili for Alisson and Endo for Ndukwe.

For Monaco, Teze for Vanderson at right-back.

It has been revealed that much to admire in that first-half performance from Liverpool’s front six and centre-backs, the latter two particularly out of possession and winning it back. The man-to-man system is working well for them. But they should be out of sight by now instead of leading by only a goal.

Liverpool free-kick on the right after a foul on Koumas. Szoboszlai whips in the cross and Van Dijk gets up first to the left of the penalty spot but bludgeons his header about a foot wide of the right post.

Charlie Adam states the penalty was ‘a soft one’ but Van Dijk did not adjust when Golovin shifted it to his right, stuck out a leg and Golovim understandably decided to topple over the hurdle.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 1 (Golovin, pen) Speared it into the top right. Alisson went the right way but was beaten for pace and power.

The referee, Jarred Gillett, gives Monaco a penalty. It was deserved, too. Golovin went on a driving run down the middle, shifted it to his right and was tripped by Van Dijk.

According to recent reports, liverpool are well worth their lead. They are streets ahead of Monaco.

A microcosm of the game so far: Liverpool pass goes astray, a player wins it back – this time Gakpo – by snapping into a tackle before laying it off to his left for the unmarked Tsimikas to skim a low shot about a foot wide of the left post from 25 yards.

Monaco have done very little since that wee salvo in the opening minute but just now Abline was given too much space from distance but whacked his shot into the Kop.

Significant cheer from the crowd for Hugo Ekitike.

The impressive Koumas diddles Nazinho with a Cruyff turn but then thumps his shot straight into Hradecky’s chest.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 0 (Wirtz) Pass chipped out to Koumas down the right who arcs a cross to the back post. Gakpo meets it with a header back across goal to Isak whose first effort from a couple of yards is blocked but the ball gets stuck under Isak’s falling body and Wirtz is Johnny on the Spot to stab it in from a 18 inches as Dier tried to scramble it away.

Liverpool have been impressive so far but if there has been a weakness it’s still the balance in central midfield defensively. Going forward both Gravenberch and Szobiszlai have dovetailed together well. They win the ball back when Van Dijk steps out and the midfield two fly forward to tee up Koumas for a shot that strikes Dier.

Chance for Wirtz, who opens his body from the left of the D to try to bend a shot into the bottom right corner but fizzes it the wrong side of the post.

It’s been pretty breathless since the goal, Liverpool dozily letting Monaco through the middle before twice cutting Monaco apart in midfield only for Isak to overrun a pass in the box delivered by Wirtz and then Koumas to shoot over.

It has been revealed that liverpool 1 Monaco 0 (Isak) Chip to Gakpo down the left of the box, he clips it first time back to Gravenberch in the D who lays it off to Szoboszlai. Ping-ping-ping. Szoboszlai keeps the tempo high with return, the one in the one-two with Gravenberch who picks out Isak to bury a shot from about 15 yards into the bottom left corner.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz.

It has been revealed that excellent move from Liverpool, instigated by Ndukwe’s fine tackle on Biereth. He knocks it short to Gravenberch who arrows a 60-yard pass out to Koumas hurtling down the right. He measures his cross perfectly for Gakpo stealing in off the left wing and though he connects powerfully with the meat of his brow, he bashes it straight at the keeper. He was offside in any case, it transpires.

Charlie Adam on co-comms points out that Liverpool are going man-to-man now in classic Iraola/Bielsa style and when the camera goes high you can see it, especially with the full-backs.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool are carving the middle of the park up with incisive passing. Szoboszlai starts a move that sends Isak down the left of the box. He traps the chip, turns back to face away from goal and taps a pass back to Wirtz who gallops on to it and bends a shot that Hradecky dives low to his left to beat away with a firm left wrist. Frimpong pounces on the rebound and clips a tame effort straight at Hradecky who had quickly restored himself to the vertical.

Van Dijk gobbles up a long pass over Ndukwe, snuffing out any possibility of Biereth getting there first.

It has been revealed that tsimikas is free down the left but overhits his cross on the run when Isak was begging for a cut-back. The left-back went for the back post and ballooned his centre behind, miles beyond Koumas and Wirtz.

It has been revealed that liverpool defend the corner solidly and Frimpong races away on the counter, bombing on to the ball and sprinting into the Monaco half. But his touch is not as sound as his pace and Monaco deal with him when he fluffs his control.

A period of applause in memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AkPZG7babe.

In a recent development, liverpool kick off defending the Kop. They roll the ball back to Frimpong who chips a long pass up the right to Koumas who hares on to the pass down the right and crosses, just beyond Isak. Hradecky gathers and bowls the ball out. A mistake by Tisimikas lets Biereth barrel through the inside-right to hammer a shot that Alisson turns behind for a corner.

The crowd applauds in the modern way. My goodness he was a terrific player. Saw him play for Liverpool, Southampton and Newcastle. Absolutely relentless.

Industry observers note that virgil van Dijk has the pennant. Liverpool are wearing all red with the paint splashes of the 1990 kit. Monaco are in a very pale green.

For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

Sources indicate that I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

It has been revealed that I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

According to recent reports, 🥳 Feliz aniversário, 𝐅𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐩𝐞 𝐋𝐮𝐢́𝐬! 🎉Notre coach fête aujourd'hui ses 41 ans 🎂 pic.twitter.com/VTd4BQ5rRK.

Alisson, Van Dijk and Gakpo return, Ndukwe continues in defence.

The Reds to take on AS Monaco at Anfield!Watch the match LIVE on All Red Video 📺.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

This afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under new management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

Recent findings suggest that in pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

Equally great are both the transparency modes, which pump in outside sounds while you're wearing your AirPods, and Adaptive Transparency, which automatically adjusts the level of transparency based on how loud or soft your surroundings are. This is a great mode for wearing your AirPods in loud environments, so you can still hear everything without the noise becoming overwhelming. To that point, these AirPods are actually FDA-certified hearing aids.

In a recent development, there are plenty of other features available here as well, especially if you have a compatible iPhone. AirPods Pro 3 have a built-in heart rate sensor, so you can track workouts without an Apple Watch; you can translate conversations in real time with Live Translate; "Conversation Awareness" lowers the volume of your audio and turns on transparency mode when you start speaking; and they run for eight hours on one charge with noise cancellation enabled.

Industry observers note that this isn't an in-depth list of the AirPods Pro 3's set of features. But suffice it to say, these earbuds are worth their full MSRP of $249. So not only can I wholeheartedly recommend them at $149, but I'd say they're an easy buy if you've been thinking about picking up AirPods for yourself.

In a recent development, the FBI franchise may be bracing for change once again after the most recent episodes explored one of its longest standing characters leaving Newly introduced York, but the CBS series is creating the perfect conditions to revive one of its most intense franchise demonstrates. Throughout the run of FBI, the Dick Wolf series has spun off into several different shows, building an expanded universe that has been scaled back in recent years. FBI has spun off into FBI: Most Wanted in 2020, FBI: International in 2021, and most recently, CIA in early 2026, bringing viewers into several different teams that have crossover potential.

According to recent reports, FBI: Most Wanted, which was led by the late Julian McMahon for its first three seasons before Dylan McDermott took over in the final three years, had a tough time getting on its feet, but managed to be one of the most interesting spinoffs the franchise ever had. Exploring the work of the Fugitive Task Force, Most Wanted saw its team searching out criminals on the Most Wanted list who were intense, dangerous, and at times, terrifying. Eventually, including Shantel VanSanten's Nina Chase, FBI and FBI: Most Wanted connected in an interesting way when Chase and FBI's Stuart Scola's (John Boyd) crossover romance came into play.

Sources indicate that when Most Wanted came to a close, one of the biggest questions was about whether Nina and Scola's relationship would be able to continue, especially considering how deeply they'd connected. Now, with the pair married and parents to a young son, Dougie, Nina's move to San Diego to lead a brand new task force sets up the perfect conditions for the return of FBI: Most Wanted.

With Nina and Scola working through her move to San Diego in the past few episodes of the series, the pair appeared together during FBI season 9 episode 7, "Posterity," and made it clear that their priority was their family. While both agents are dedicated to their work and want to explore further opportunities with the FBI, Scola began to realize he wasn't interested in living fully across the country from his wife and son. Sharing that he put in for a transfer that won't go through for some time, Scola's likely to find himself leaving the Latest York FBI office to join his family.

While Scola's departure hasn't been set in stone or given a time frame yet, it's clear that he's serious about moving away from the city to be with Nina and Dougie, which sets up the perfect conditions for a new FBI spinoff. With CIA having joined the FBI family in 2026, the lack of spinoffs right now airing within the franchise leaves some space for what's to come on, and with minimal coverage on the West Coast, an FBI spinoff anchored by two well-known figures in the franchise could be a huge swing for the CBS hit.

It has been revealed that while there hasn't been any movement on what could happen with a Scola and Nina FBI spinoff, the fact that they're moving away from the original series in the future opens up something vastly different for the franchise. Branching out to San Diego and following Nina's task force, Scola's transition into a latest place, or both could allow FBI to shift its scope within one of the franchise's shows. A West Coast series could combine the approaches of FBI and FBI: Most Wanted, creating something that looks and feels like a franchise series, but has different, unexpected beats for viewers to follow.

Though Nina and Scola would be the anchoring characters for a spinoff, a series that follows them to the West Coast would have to avoid becoming too consistently about their relationship. Regardless of the potential pitfalls, another FBI franchise spinoff that brings back the higher stakes of Most Wanted while being able to keep two of the franchise's best agents in the spotlight feels like a no-brainer. Ultimately, CBS has the chance to chase the appeal of what made FBI: Most Wanted work throughout its six-season run, and at the same time, keep a wonderful FBI pair together in a newly introduced setting.

The TCL QM64L is a solid compact budget Mini-LED TV. It brings great HDR performance, vibrant colors and details, smooth gaming and an improved Fire TV experience. However, you should expect lower black levels, slight blooming and weaker speakers than higher-priced models.

Compact design for small spaces.

Punchy detail in colors, natural skin tones.

Sources indicate that why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Not everyone has room in their home or dorm room setup for the best 65-inch TVs so finding a smaller, budget-friendly TV that can make movies and shows look great can be challenging. Cheaper TVs can suffer from poor brightness, picture quality, and the smart TV software can be slow and sluggish. The TCL QM64L excels against its rivals in a lot of these categories.

Sporting a sleek, redesigned Fire TV interface and a Mini-LED panel capable of delivering great HDR performance with vibrant colors and natural-looking skin tones, this is a TV that really impresses for its price — $599 for a 65-inch model on Black Friday.

Both in my lab testing and hands-on time, the TCL QM64L consistently delivered an enjoyable viewing experience. However, its compact size and budget-friendly price come with some compromises, including poor black levels, slight blooming around bright highlights and bad downward-firing speakers.

The TCL QM64L might not be taking down mid-tier and high-end flagship TVs when you compare its raw specs and our lab test results, but for budget-conscious buyers who want a small compact TV without breaking the bank, it will deliver a great everyday viewing experience.

The TCL QM64L comes in multiple sizes, starting at 50 inches. You can’t buy the 50-inch size directly from TCL, but third-party retailers like Amazon carry the 50-inch size that we reviewed.

Pricing starts at $499 for the 50-inch model, and goes as high as $2,199 for a 98-inch model. When on sale, you can grab the 50-inch model for $429, and the 98-inch model for $1,699. Full pricing for the range can be seen below.

QD-Mini-LED QLED with Full-Array Local Dimming.

Dolby Vision (including Dolby Vision IQ), HDR10+, HDR10, and HLG.

144Hz native refresh rate (HDMI 1, 2), 60Hz (HDMI 3,4).

4x HDMI 2.1, 1x USB-A 3.0, 1x USB-A 2.0, ATSC,SPDIF Digital Audio Optical port.

Like many budget TVs, there’s nothing fancy about the design of the TCL QM64L. The only highlight would be its super thin bezels which come in at around a quarter of an inch thick. It also is made of plastic, with legs that attach at a curved angle to support the bottom of the TV. Up front, there’s a silver lip on the bottom of the panel for the TCL logo.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

It has been revealed that I would have loved for this set to feature center-facing legs like some of its competitors, since that would help save even more space in a tight-packed room. This is not a huge dealbreaker, though, since this TV is already so compact.

According to recent reports, what I love the most is that TCL packs in four HDMI 2.1 ports. Two of them — HDMI 1 and HDMI 2 — can output 4K at 144Hz, but the other two are capped at 60Hz. Having two 144Hz ports is nice, especially if you’re a gamer, since you can connect two consoles to the TV. The other ports on the TV include one USB 3.0 port and one USB 2.0 port, as well as the ATSC port, and a SPDIF Digital Audio Optical port.

Industry observers note that whether I was watching “Spider-Man: No Way Home” on our lab’s Blu-Ray player, streaming “Cross” on Amazon Prime Video, or watching a simple SDR aquarium video on YouTube, the Mini-LED panel on this TV produced punchy highlights and plenty of visual pop. However, the weaker black levels and some slight blooming in very specific scenes prevent it from delivering what you might get from a more premium and larger TV.

With “Spider-Man: No Way Home” in Filmmaker Mode, the TCL QM64L was great with fine details, natural skin tones and vibrant colors. Tom Holland’s shirt sported a clean, vibrant blue, while fine details like his facial scar and Zendaya’s red lipstick remained sharp. The TV struggled a bit with overall black levels in the details in the Sanctum Sanctorum undercroft, though. The blacks in Norman Osborne’s jacket and the brickwork felt slightly muted and gray.

It has been revealed that in later fight scenes, slight blooming also flared around Spider-Man’s hands as they glowed against dark backgrounds. Punchy silver accents and a shiny gold spider emblem in his Black and Gold Suit, however, proved that the QM64L delivers plenty of visual pop.

When streaming HDR content on Amazon Prime Video, the TCL QM64L wowed me right from the opening seconds in the first episode of “Cross.” Facial textures were impressively rendered, revealing crisp individual strands of beard hair on Cross’s face with that I almost feel the urge to reach out and straighten them.

To my surprise, the QM64L also handled rapid brightness shifts with ease. It seamlessly transitioned from the shadowy, low-light interior of an interrogation room to a dim, moody tunnel intro and then burst into a punchy, bright outdoor shot of the Washington, D.C. skyline.

Industry observers note that finally, switching over to a SDR aquarium video on YouTube, the TCL QM64L continued to impress with its vibrant color handling. As a clownfish navigated through lush pink coral reefs the distinctive white stripe on the clownfish's head popped with crisp, clean brightness against its orange body. This proves that this budget display handles underwater marine scenes with surprising depth and visual punch.

Recent findings suggest that across all tests, the 50-inch TCL QM64L delivers surprisingly impressive picture quality for a budget TV. It brings out crisp fine details, natural-looking skin tones and vibrant colors across SDR and HDR content.

Roku 65-inch Class Select Series 4K QLED (2026).

Vizio Mini-LED Quantum 4K Smart TV 65-inch VQM65-C.

Roku Pro OLED TV 65-inch (Measurements with "Brighter".

I lab-tested the TCL QM64L in filmmaker mode alongside five notable rivals in its class, including the LED-driven Sony Bravia 3 II (65-inch), the the Hisense 65M7SR, the Roku 65-inch Class Select Series 4K QLED (2026), the Vizio Mini-LED Quantum 4K Smart TV 65-inch, and the premium Roku Pro OLED TV 65-inch.

Industry observers note that there’s no doubt that this TV will trail its mid-tier and higher-end competitors in raw benchmarking. It is not going to hit high levels of brightness and color accuracy or performance like a flagship might. However, at this price, it is still a surprisingly bright budget TV.

According to recent reports, when it comes to the 10% SDR window measurement, which shows you how bright a TV gets with cable TV and everyday content, the Hisense 65M7SR is the best of the bunch at 466 nits. The TCL QM64L follows at 359 nits, and Sony Bravia 3 II hits 352 nits while the Roku Select Series (334 nits) also comes close to that group. The flagship Roku Pro OLED comes in at 330 nits, while the Vizio Mini-LED Quantum trails the group at 218 nits.

My lab assistant and I personally test every TV across SDR and HDR benchmarks using the 10% window method. For color accuracy, we set the TV to Filmmaker Mode, usually the “best” mode on the TV first. We also disable any ambient light sensors that could skew our meter’s readings.

In a recent development, for our tools, we use the Jeti spectraval 1501-HiRes spectroradiometer to profile the Klein K10-A colorimeter. Once profiled, these work with the Murideo 8K-SIX-G Metal pattern generator and a Tom’s-Guide specific workflow in Portrait Displays’ Calman Ultimate software which helps us determine the TV’s overall brightness and color accuracy across HDR and SDR.

In a recent development, we use a Leo Bodnar 4K Video Signal Lag Tester with the TV’s Game Mode to measure how responsive the TV really is. Once all lab testing is done, we put the TV through subjective testing using a curated selection of films and shows, both on streaming services and on our lab’s Blu-ray player.

Visit our “How we test TVs” guide for a more in-depth explanation on the process.

According to recent reports, for HDR content, the TCL QM64L shines best with 630 nits in our 10% window test. That puts it ahead of every TV in this comparison group except the Vizio Mini-LED Quantum, which leads at 781 nits.

Sources indicate that color accuracy out of the box in Filmmaker mode is where the TCL QM64L is a little weak. Our lab measured a Delta-E score of 3.3, where lower numbers are better.

With SDR color performance, the TCL fell behind everything except the Roku Select Series, although its results are still respectable considering the prices.

When looking at the UHDA-P3 HDR color gamut coverage, which is how most HDR content is presented, the TCL again fell toward the bottom of the back, only just edging out the Roku Select Series once again.

When it came to the more demanding Rec. 2020 spectrum, the TCL moved up slightly, trailing only the Sony Bravia 3 II and Roku Select Series.

The TCL scored a low result in our input latency tests (13 milliseconds) that put it at the bottom of our test results list, but don't let that fool you: I still enjoyed the gaming experience.

Overall, when battling through a boss fight in Marvel’s Wolverine, I did not experience any lag in my inputs. I also tried playing Sonic Superstars. In this fast-paced game, rolling around collecting coins was fun and super smooth..

Industry observers note that like more premium TVs, TCL bundles in support for VRR, ALLM and Game Accelerator with a Game Bar. All of this meant that when I pressed the menu button on the remote, I could pull up a Game Bar to fine-tune the TV for my gameplay.

Sources indicate that features like Game Picture Mode, Shadow Enhancement, and Aiming Aid can spice up the gaming experience. My personal favorite was the Floating Window option, and High Frame Rate mode, which helped me keep track of the frames when playing Marvel’s Wolverine on our lab’s PlayStation 5.

As mentioned earlier, the TCL QM64L has two HDMI 2.1 ports that support refresh rates of 144Hz; in comparison, the Sony Bravia 3 II and the Roku Pro Series both have four HDMI 2.1 ports, but refresh rates are capped at 120Hz.

In a recent development, budget TVs have to make some sacrifices, and one of those is the sound setup. The TCL QM64L sports two 10W speakers on the underside front. With the TV sitting on a table, I didn’t quite enjoy the way it handled audio.

While watching “Spider-Man: No Way Home” on our lab’s Blu-ray player, the dialog presentation felt a little muted and muffled from afar. I was forced to push the volume up into the 20s just to make out dialogue clearly.

Sources indicate that listening to "Flower in a Hurricane," from the “Grand Theft Auto 6” trailer, the opening guitars and electronic beats did have some impressive detail and spatial depth. However, as soon as the drum beats kicked in, the bass sounded tinny, hollow, and largely absent.

Pick up one of the best soundbars to upgrade this TV's audio.

It has been revealed that one of my biggest complaints about the previous Fire TV interface found on many budget TVs was how outdated it looked, with a giant ad taking up the top of the screen and the navigation bar awkwardly positioned in the middle. Thankfully, Amazon has given its interface a much-needed makeover. The newly redesigned Fire TV OS that came on the QM64L as an out of the box update is super clean, speedy, and brings it up to par with what I’ve seen on other SmartTV platforms this year.

In a recent development, the navigation bar now sits at the top of the screen, with clearly labeled sections for profile, search, home, movies, TV Shows, live, sports and news. It's a much more intuitive layout that I’ve long enjoyed on Google TV and even Samsung’s Tizen OS.

Of course, the ads are still there. Show recommendations and promotional content now take up the space where the old navigation bar used to sit. There's also a dedicated Apps and Channels section, making it easier to jump straight into your favorite streaming services.

The redesigned interface feels more fluid. I frequently dive into the picture settings when testing TVs, and I appreciate how the upcoming menus use a gray background with white highlights to make it easier to see which setting you're adjusting. It's a small change, but one that makes the interface feel considerably more polished.

This TV also has a cool ambient mode that displays artwork when you're not actively watching something. It's a nice touch that gives the QM64L a little more personality when it's not in use. I love it, and I am sure students putting this TV in a dorm room will too.

The remote included with this TV is nothing fancy. While it is backlit, it has the same standard layout as many remotes that come with TCL’s other TVs. I like the dedicated play and pause button, as well as the buttons for accessing the settings, and Netflix and YouTube. A programmable button would have been nice, but you can’t expect that for this price.

The TCL QM64L is a great 50-inch TV. For budget-conscious buyers, the QM64L delivers where it counts most. Its Mini-LED brightness, attention to fine details, and sleek Fire TV OS helps it stand out as one of the best compact TV values for small living rooms, bedrooms, or dorm setups.

The biggest rival would be the Hisense 65M7SR with its better SDR brightness, slightly more accurate out-of-box color performance, and slightly wider color gamut coverage than the TCL QM64L. While it can't match the TCL's HDR brightness, it's just as compelling an option if you prefer the Roku TV experience and want to prioritize overall color performance over bright HDR.

The QM64L’s budget price tag does come with clear trade-offs like muted, grayish blacks, and slight blooming around bright objects in dark scenes. The downward-firing speakers also deliver hollow audio with muddy dialogue, making a soundbar an essential purchase.

While it is more expensive, the Sony Bravia 3 II still serves as a major step up from this TCL thanks to Sony's superior image processing and color accuracy. Finally, if your main goal is better HDR brightness in a sunlit room, the Vizio Mini-LED Quantum will be for you.

Of course, if budget isn't a strict constraint and you want to completely eliminate blooming with infinite contrast and pristine color, stepping up to an OLED like the Roku Pro Series OLED is the ultimate fix for many of these TVs problems, though it comes at a higher cost.

But, if you're looking for an affordable set under $500, the TCL QM64L could be just the ticket.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, bellisario hasn't been creatively involved with NCIS in years, departing after Season 4 amid reported creative differences with Harmon.
  • The sale is notable because of how popular the series still is.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Donald P. Bellisario created the military legal drama procedural JAG over 30 years ago, he couldn't have had any idea what kind of juggernaut franchise he was spawning. The prolific Emmy nominee had a hand in creating his fair share of iconic television series, including the original Magnum P.I. starring Tom Selleck, and Quantum Leap, but the three-letter acronym has cast the longest shadow thanks to the much bigger giant that would come out of it — NCIS. While the parent series would go on to last for ten seasons on CBS, the decision to introduce Leroy Jethro Gibbs (Mark Harmon) and the Major Case Response Team cemented its place in television history. Now, after over 500 episodes and seven spin-offs across over 23 years, he's bowing out completely.

In a recent development, bellisario hasn't been creatively involved with NCIS in years, departing after Season 4 amid reported creative differences with Harmon. However, none of it would exist without him and Don McGill, and as such, he's remained financially attached to the series. In 2013, CBS even settled a lawsuit with the co-creator after he claimed his contract required him to be offered either a "first opportunity” to work on NCIS: Los Angeles when it was originated, or payments related to the spin-off. According to a Bloomberg newsletter, though, Bellisario recently sold off his share of the back end on NCIS for somewhere around $400 million.

The sale is notable because of how popular the series still is. Just this fall, the mothership and two of its three current spin-offs, NCIS: Fresh York and NCIS: Origins, premiered their latest seasons to an average of 5.49 million viewers, making it the most-watched broadcast slate of the evening and a resurgence for the entire brand. All three continue to be ratings winners, too, thanks in part to a season energized by the return of some of the most familiar faces in the procedural universe, like Harmon, Michael Weatherly, and LL COOL J. Ongoing revenue from the franchise was earning Bellisario over $25 million per year before he decided to sell.

In a recent development, network television is no stranger to long-running procedurals that can survive beyond the exits of stars and creatives and blossom into entire universes, but few can quite rival the sheer size and scale of NCIS. Only the original Law & Order and its spin-off, Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, have run for more seasons, with Grey's Anatomy the only other to eclipse the 20-season mark. Still, CBS put quite a staggering number on the franchise's overall success — $10 billion. That's how much the network revealed NCIS sales have earned since its inception, between advertising, merchandise, licensing, and more.

According to recent reports, skydance TV co-chair George Cheeks told Bloomberg that it "dwarfs" many streaming series when digging into the numbers, calling it CBS' "quiet hero" when all is said and done. It's not losing any momentum either, with the newest spin-off, NCIS: Fresh York, debuting as the most-watched new program of the fall television season.

Recent findings suggest that the NCIS franchise continues to air on Tuesdays starting at 8 p.m. ET/PT on CBS. Stay tuned here at Collider for more on the future of the franchise and its spin-offs.
