📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that most people are probably waiting until Jan. 1 to start getting in shape, whether they want to start fresh or absolve themselves of their perceived holiday indulgences. Every year, people start the new year by joining a gym crowded with others newly resolved to get in shape, paying full price for the privilege of waiting in a long line to use the squat rack. This year, try something different: Start your gym membership during Black Friday.

According to recent reports, the week of Black Friday can deliver you a good discount on a gym membership, an empty gym, and a built-in two-month runway to turn a generic resolution into a real habit. While you're comparing deals on new tech, headphones, or smart home devices, here’s why you should also take a few minutes to scout out the gyms near you.

This week is as good a time to save of a gym membership as a newly introduced air fryer. Here are just a few examples of the offers out there right now:.

Orangetheory and F45 have various free-month and prize-entry promotions for new Black Friday sign-ups, and similar studios for Pilates, yoga, and strength training have discounted multi-month and annual packages.

Independent gyms, university rec centers, and local studios often run their own versions, from a free month tacked onto a longer commitment to waived joining fees.

Deals vary a lot by location, so call or stop by the clubs near you and ask what's available. Then remember to always read the fine print before you sign:.

Look at the price after the promotion ends, not just the first month's rate.

Ask about fees, including joining, annual, and access fees.

In a recent development, try before you buy. Many gyms offer a free trial pass. It might make sense to first visit at the time of day you'd actually go.

According to recent reports, be honest about distance. The best gym is the one you'll actually walk into, so pick one that's close to home or work.

Gyms also run sales around New Year's, so a good Black Friday offer isn't the only deal you'll see. Even still, the savings aren't the only reason to go now.

December is reliably the quietest stretch of the gym year: People are busy with holiday travel and work deadlines, and many tell themselves they'll "start fresh in January." That means open benches, free treadmills, and staff who have time to show you how a machine works.

That's a gift for any gym-goer, but especially if you're new. Learning your way around a gym is much less intimidating when it's empty. You can figure out the equipment, make your mistakes in peace, and build a routine before the January crowds arrive. Plus, this time of year is a perfect window to set and achieve a winnable goal.

According to recent reports, from Black Friday to Fresh Year's Day is about five weeks. By the time the January rush hits its peak and settles into its usual patterns, you could be eight weeks into a new routine. And as my colleague Beth Skwarecki explains, you really can get a lot stronger in 24 workouts. Beginners tend to see the fastest gains of their lifting lives in the first couple of months.

Industry observers note that prefer running? I know I do, and luckily, a couch-to-5K initiative works the same way. Most programs run about nine weeks and build you up gradually from short run-walk intervals. Start the week after Black Friday and you'll be running for a solid stretch by early January, and you'll be well on your way to 30 minutes at a stretch by the end of the month. By the time your Newly introduced Year's resolution friends are just starting, you'll already be a few runs in.

This is also the season when many workplaces and health prepares wrap up their open enrollment periods, which makes it a smart time to check what wellness perks you already have. Before you pay full price for anything, look into:.

Workplace wellness programs, which sometimes offer gym reimbursements, discounted memberships or fitness stipends.

Health insurance perks, since some aims include gym memberships or discounts.

HSA and FSA rules, where general gym memberships usually don't qualify, but some medically recommended programs may. Also check any year-end deadlines for money you'd otherwise lose.

Corporate and employer discounts, which many large gyms offer on top of regular promotions.

Stack a workplace benefit on top of a holiday sale, and your cost per workout can drop considerably—well before Latest Year's resolution time arrives.

Why Chris Pratt Chose Way Of The Warrior Kid For His Next Movie Explained By The Star

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, based on Jocko Willink's children's book, Way of the Warrior Kid is a family-friendly throwback to the best of '80s cinema, and thus ironically makes perfect sense as Chris Pratt's next movie between seasons of The Terminal List.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, based on Jocko Willink's children's book, Way of the Warrior Kid is a family-friendly throwback to the best of '80s cinema, and thus ironically makes perfect sense as Chris Pratt's next movie between seasons of The Terminal List. While both projects see him playing Navy SEALs, the tone of each could not be more different. Directed by McG from a screenplay by Will Staples, the newly introduced Apple TV movie is more akin to The Karate Kid than to Pratt's hit Prime Video series.

According to recent reports, way of the Warrior Kid follows Marc (Jude Hill), a young boy fresh out of eighth grade who yearns to leave the days of being bullied behind once he reaches high school. His mother, Sarah (Linda Cardellini), hopes that an extended visit from his uncle, Jake (Pratt), will provide Marc with the guidance he needs to flourish. Jake is dealing with his own demons after his most recent SEAL Team mission went awry, which means that the burgeoning bond between uncle and nephew could be just what the doctor ordered for each of them.

ScreenRant's Liam Crowley interviewed the stars and author of Way of the Warrior Kid, getting a perfect play-by-play on how Pratt and Willink went beyond collaborating on products to actually bring the heartwarming film to life. Pratt also explained why he wanted to take on such a project, while Hill shared the lessons he's taken from film set experiences as a child and teenager.

Recent findings suggest that screenRant: It's a significant year for Chris Pratt playing Navy SEALs. I feel like Uncle Jake is the antithesis of The Terminal List's James Reece. James had his family taken away from him. Uncle Jake is kind of forced into being a father figure in this film. Did you feel that way when filming?

It has been revealed that chris Pratt: It's a really funny point. Yeah, you're right. I've played with a lot of Navy SEALs, especially this past year. And you're right; I think it speaks to the difference in tone of the type of film that we made with Way of the Warrior Kid. This is a feel-good family movie geared towards younger kids.

According to recent reports, in something like The Terminal List, obviously our north star is authenticity and grit. We're making a psychological thriller and an action thriller. But in this film, we're trying to root it in the reality and the heart of a relationship between a man and a boy. So, it's a little bit different. I don't know that the characters are actually different at all. I think just as I've always played every character, the entire set of circumstances around them and the tone and the story that they're told is different. And so I think it's the same person in a way.

ScreenRant: Jude, you've had quite the career at just 16 years old, and it's fair to say you've had a pretty unique childhood, effectively growing up on film sets. Did this filming experience teach you anything upcoming about what it's like to be a kid in today's day and age?

Jude Hill: Totally. I mean, I moved from my home country when I was about 12 or 13 years old. I was playing this American kid, and thankfully I had spent some time in a school in Florida, so I could get around the head of American kids because they're different everywhere. But yeah, you're so right. It was different for me because I hadn't really experienced it that much. So, it was nice to do a little bit of research, and then I had friends and stuff I could go to just with certain questions I had.

According to recent reports, screenRant: Chris, I understand you have a long history with Jocko specifically. It seems like you really seek out your creative partners with projects like this. How did this process with Jocko begin and make its way to launching this film?

According to recent reports, chris Pratt: Well, I'll tell you exactly how. I went to my agency, and I was discussing how it was important for me to try to find some work at home so that I could be present at home with my kids. We were talking about various promotional opportunities, and they gave me this long list of companies they're close with, and none of them really stuck. Meanwhile, I'm wearing a pair of Origin jeans and boots, and I'm drinking a Jocko Go, and I didn't see Origin or Jocko on this list. And I was like, "Listen, guys, I'm just going to actually call Jocko myself.".

So, I literally cold-called him from my house. He was up in the mountains literally training snipers at the time. I was like, "Listen, dude, we know each other. We've spent some time together." We didn't know each other that well, but I told him I want to promote things and I want it to be authentic. "I love Origin, I love Jocko Fuel, and I really just think you're great. I want to be a business together." He was like, "Sounds great. Let me finish this up, and I'll ping you back.".

Apparently, he then told that to his internal people and without his knowledge, they sent me the script. He had told me, "I'm not going to just send you the script," because it was embarrassing that he had a script written that he paid for to do a screenplay. He didn't want to be that guy that's like, "Oh, you want to go in business? Well, here's my script." But I'm glad his people did because I sat there and out of reverence for him, I opened page one.

I did not even move until I finished the entire script, and I thought it was great. I thought it was really meeting a cultural moment. I sent it to my team. I was like, "I love this movie. I think there's a way for us to do this movie." And that was the beginning of doing this movie.

It has been revealed that screenRant: Jocko, I understand you have a pretty tenured relationship with Chris Pratt. Where did this all begin?

According to recent reports, jocko Willink: Thankfully, I had some mutual friends. Jared Shaw, who was on my SEAL team, trained Chris and eventually worked on Terminal List. Jack Carr, who wrote Terminal List, I was friends with both those guys. Through those guys, I met Chris Pratt, and then Chris got interested in Jocko Fuel. He's a partner in Jocko Fuel. He's a partner in Origin USA, the clothing manufacturer I have. So, we're business partners there. And eventually he got the script for Warrior Kid. And as soon as he read the script, he remarked, "We got to make this movie.".

Industry observers note that screenRant: I understand too that Uncle Jake is largely based on your own life experience. I can imagine that's a little easy when you're writing him on the page, but when he's brought to life as Chris Pratt standing in front of the camera, did you see yourself in Chris on set?

Jocko Willink: Yeah, and it was really neat to watch. Uncle Jake is a SEAL. In the book, he's a little bit more of a superhero. He's kind of perfect in the book. In the movie, he's more realistic. He's a human being, and Chris did a great job of capturing that.

And, look, we filmed some scenes that are very powerful. The scenes up at Rosecrans National Cemetery, which is where I have my friends buried, we shot up there, and the interactions that Chris and I were having and the discussions about the emotions and what that feels like were very vital and very powerful. Chris just did an incredible job of bringing that to life in the movie.

Sources indicate that screenRant: I find that a lot of times when people have a singular purpose, whether it be as an athlete, a performer, or a Navy SEAL, your mind can get jumbled when you're removed from that. You're like, "What do I do now, because I always had just one mission moving forward?" How did you reshape your life purpose?

Sources indicate that jocko Willink: This is what I tell veterans all the time: when you get done with your military career, you have to find a new mission. And if you don't find a new mission, you're going to be lost and discombobulated. That can become problematic.

For me, as soon as I retired from the SEAL teams, I started teaching leadership to companies across the country, and then that turned into writing books, and then that turned into podcasts, and that turned into a clothing firm and a supplement company and eventually kids' books. To me, it's finding that next mission and pouring into that mission and keeping your head on a swivel and keeping your situational awareness high. So when other opportunities arrive or arise, you have to take advantage of them.

It has been revealed that screenRant: It's very interesting to do this film because you're dealing with a younger demographic. When you're writing this story, and you're bringing it to life with a child effectively, how do you reach them?

Industry observers note that jocko Willink: I have my own kids. I got four kids myself. And not only that, I was a kid, and I do remember what it was like being a kid. When I was writing Way of the Warrior Kid, I was always kind of surprised at what it said because it is really written from me as a 10-year-old. It almost feels like I didn't write it because I wrote it in the character, in the mindset of, "Hey, I'm a 10-year-old kid. I remember what this was like." That's why I think it comes across as natural because I just jumped in.

In a recent development, look, I'm not the most mature person in the world. I know I might look a little older, but I have no problem devolving into a 12-year-old sometimes and keeping that mindset. So, that's what I did when I wrote the book; I think that came through when Will wrote the screenplay, and I think that's why it worked.

#120772. Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

📅 09 Feb 2022 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2875 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The AI pioneer says it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to big concerns.
  • Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.
  • Andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The AI pioneer says it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to big concerns.

Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.

Andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence. He pioneered the use of graphics processing units (GPUs) to train deep learning models in the late 2000s with his students at Stanford University, cofounded Google Brain in 2011, and then served for three years as chief scientist for Baidu, where he helped build the Chinese tech giant’s AI group. So when he says he has identified the next big shift in artificial intelligence, people listen. And that’s what he told IEEE Spectrum in an exclusive Q&A.

Ng’s current efforts are focused on his firm Landing AI, which built a platform called LandingLens to help manufacturers improve visual inspection with computer vision. He has also become something of an evangelist for what he calls the data-centric AI movement, which he says can yield “small data” solutions to massive problems in AI, including model efficiency, accuracy, and bias.

The great advances in deep learning over the past decade or so have been powered by ever-bigger models crunching ever-bigger amounts of data. Some people argue that that’s an unsustainable trajectory. Do you agree that it can’t go on that way?

According to recent reports, andrew Ng: This is a substantial question. We’ve seen foundation models in NLP [natural language processing]. I’m excited about NLP models getting even bigger, and also about the potential of building foundation models in computer vision. I think there’s lots of signal to still be exploited in video: We have not been able to build foundation models yet for video because of compute bandwidth and the cost of processing video, as opposed to tokenized text. So I think that this engine of scaling up deep learning algorithms, which has been running for something like 15 years now, still has steam in it. Having said that, it only applies to certain problems, and there’s a set of other problems that need small data solutions.

When you say you want a foundation model for computer vision, what do you mean by that?

Ng: This is a term coined by Percy Liang and some of my friends at Stanford to refer to very large models, trained on very large data sets, that can be tuned for specific applications. For example, GPT-3 is an example of a foundation model [for NLP]. Foundation models offer a lot of promise as a upcoming paradigm in developing machine learning applications, but also challenges in terms of making sure that they’re reasonably fair and free from bias, especially if many of us will be building on top of them.

What needs to happen for someone to build a foundation model for video?

In a recent development, ng: I think there is a scalability problem. The compute power needed to process the large volume of images for video is significant, and I think that’s why foundation models have arisen first in NLP. Many researchers are working on this, and I think we’re seeing early signs of such models being developed in computer vision. But I’m confident that if a semiconductor maker gave us 10 times more processor power, we could easily find 10 times more video to build such models for vision.

In a recent development, having said that, a lot of what’s happened over the past decade is that deep learning has happened in consumer-facing companies that have large user bases, sometimes billions of users, and therefore very large data sets. While that paradigm of machine learning has driven a lot of economic value in consumer software, I find that that recipe of scale doesn’t work for other industries.

It’s funny to hear you say that, because your early work was at a consumer-facing company with millions of people.

Ng: Over a decade ago, when I proposed starting the Google Brain project to use Google’s compute infrastructure to build very large neural networks, it was a controversial step. One very senior person pulled me aside and warned me that starting Google Brain would be bad for my career. I think he felt that the action couldn’t just be in scaling up, and that I should instead focus on architecture innovation.

“In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from substantial data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.” —Andrew Ng, CEO & Founder, Landing AI.

I remember when my students and I published the first NeurIPS workshop paper advocating using CUDA, a platform for processing on GPUs, for deep learning—a different senior person in AI sat me down and said, “CUDA is really complicated to program. As a programming paradigm, this seems like too much work.” I did manage to convince him; the other person I did not convince.

I expect they’re both convinced now.

According to recent reports, over the past year as I’ve been speaking to people about the data-centric AI movement, I’ve been getting flashbacks to when I was speaking to people about deep learning and scalability 10 or 15 years ago. In the past year, I’ve been getting the same mix of “there’s nothing fresh here” and “this seems like the wrong direction.”.

How do you define data-centric AI, and why do you consider it a movement?

Recent findings suggest that ng: Data-centric AI is the discipline of systematically engineering the data needed to successfully build an AI system. For an AI system, you have to implement some algorithm, say a neural network, in code and then train it on your data set. The dominant paradigm over the last decade was to download the data set while you focus on improving the code. Thanks to that paradigm, over the last decade deep learning networks have improved significantly, to the point where for a lot of applications the code—the neural network architecture—is basically a solved problem. So for many practical applications, it’s now more productive to hold the neural network architecture fixed, and instead find ways to improve the data.

When I started speaking about this, there were many practitioners who, completely appropriately, raised their hands and said, “Yes, we’ve been doing this for 20 years.” This is the time to take the things that some individuals have been doing intuitively and make it a systematic engineering discipline.

The data-centric AI movement is much bigger than one company or group of researchers. My collaborators and I organized a data-centric AI workshop at NeurIPS, and I was really delighted at the number of authors and presenters that demonstrated up.

Industry observers note that you often talk about companies or institutions that have only a small amount of data to work with. How can data-centric AI help them?

Recent findings suggest that ng: You hear a lot about vision systems built with millions of images—I once built a face recognition system using 350 million images. Architectures built for hundreds of millions of images don’t work with only 50 images. But it turns out, if you have 50 really good examples, you can build something valuable, like a defect-inspection system. In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from big data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.

When you talk about training a model with just 50 images, does that really mean you’re taking an existing model that was trained on a very large data set and fine-tuning it? Or do you mean a brand latest model that’s designed to learn only from that small data set?

Ng: Let me describe what Landing AI does. When doing visual inspection for manufacturers, we often use our own flavor of RetinaNet. It is a pretrained model. Having said that, the pretraining is a small piece of the puzzle. What’s a bigger piece of the puzzle is providing tools that enable the manufacturer to pick the right set of images [to use for fine-tuning] and label them in a consistent way. There’s a very practical problem we’ve seen spanning vision, NLP, and speech, where even human annotators don’t agree on the appropriate label. For major data applications, the common response has been: If the data is noisy, let’s just get a lot of data and the algorithm will average over it. But if you can develop tools that flag where the data’s inconsistent and give you a very targeted way to improve the consistency of the data, that turns out to be a more efficient way to get a high-performing system.

“Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.” —Andrew Ng.

According to recent reports, for example, if you have 10,000 images where 30 images are of one class, and those 30 images are labeled inconsistently, one of the things we do is build tools to draw your attention to the subset of data that’s inconsistent. So you can very rapidly relabel those images to be more consistent, and this leads to improvement in performance.

According to recent reports, could this focus on high-quality data help with bias in data sets? If you’re able to curate the data more before training?

Recent findings suggest that ng: Very much so. Many researchers have pointed out that biased data is one factor among many leading to biased systems. There have been many thoughtful efforts to engineer the data. At the NeurIPS workshop, Olga Russakovsky gave a really nice talk on this. At the main NeurIPS conference, I also really enjoyed Mary Gray’s presentation, which touched on how data-centric AI is one piece of the solution, but not the entire solution. New tools like Datasheets for Datasets also seem like an important piece of the puzzle.

One of the powerful tools that data-centric AI gives us is the ability to engineer a subset of the data. Imagine training a machine-learning system and finding that its performance is okay for most of the data set, but its performance is biased for just a subset of the data. If you try to change the whole neural network architecture to improve the performance on just that subset, it’s quite difficult. But if you can engineer a subset of the data you can address the problem in a much more targeted way.

When you talk about engineering the data, what do you mean exactly?

It has been revealed that ng: In AI, data cleaning is notable, but the way the data has been cleaned has often been in very manual ways. In computer vision, someone may visualize images through a Jupyter notebook and maybe spot the problem, and maybe fix it. But I’m excited about tools that allow you to have a very large data set, tools that draw your attention swiftly and efficiently to the subset of data where, say, the labels are noisy. Or to quickly bring your attention to the one class among 100 classes where it would benefit you to collect more data. Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.

For example, I once figured out that a speech-recognition system was performing poorly when there was car noise in the background. Knowing that allowed me to collect more data with car noise in the background, rather than trying to collect more data for everything, which would have been expensive and slow.

What about using synthetic data, is that often a good solution?

Ng: I think synthetic data is an key tool in the tool chest of data-centric AI. At the NeurIPS workshop, Anima Anandkumar gave a great talk that touched on synthetic data. I think there are important uses of synthetic data that go beyond just being a preprocessing step for increasing the data set for a learning algorithm. I’d love to see more tools to let developers use synthetic data generation as part of the closed loop of iterative machine learning development.

Do you mean that synthetic data would allow you to try the model on more data sets?

Ng: Not really. Here’s an example. Let’s say you’re trying to detect defects in a smartphone casing. There are many different types of defects on smartphones. It could be a scratch, a dent, pit marks, discoloration of the material, other types of blemishes. If you train the model and then find through error analysis that it’s doing well overall but it’s performing poorly on pit marks, then synthetic data generation allows you to address the problem in a more targeted way. You could generate more data just for the pit-mark category.

According to recent reports, “In the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion users. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models.” —Andrew Ng.

Sources indicate that synthetic data generation is a very powerful tool, but there are many simpler tools that I will often try first. Such as data augmentation, improving labeling consistency, or just asking a factory to collect more data.

To make these complications more concrete, can you walk me through an example? When a firm approaches Landing AI and says it has a problem with visual inspection, how do you onboard them and work toward deployment?

Ng: When a customer approaches us we usually have a conversation about their inspection problem and look at a few images to verify that the problem is feasible with computer vision. Assuming it is, we ask them to upload the data to the LandingLens platform. We often advise them on the methodology of data-centric AI and help them label the data.

One of the foci of Landing AI is to empower manufacturing companies to do the machine learning work themselves. A lot of our work is making sure the software is fast and easy to use. Through the iterative process of machine learning development, we advise customers on things like how to train models on the platform, when and how to improve the labeling of data so the performance of the model improves. Our training and software supports them all the way through deploying the trained model to an edge device in the factory.

Sources indicate that how do you deal with changing needs? If products change or lighting conditions change in the factory, can the model keep up?

Ng: It varies by manufacturer. There is data drift in many contexts. But there are some manufacturers that have been running the same manufacturing line for 20 years now with few changes, so they don’t expect changes in the next five years. Those stable environments make things easier. For other manufacturers, we provide tools to flag when there’s a significant data-drift issue. I find it really key to empower manufacturing customers to correct data, retrain, and revision the model. Because if something changes and it’s 3 a.m. in the United States, I want them to be able to adapt their learning algorithm right away to maintain operations.

In the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion consumers. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models. The challenge is, how do you do that without Landing AI having to hire 10,000 machine learning specialists?

So you’re saying that to make it scale, you have to empower customers to do a lot of the training and other work.

In a recent development, ng: Yes, exactly! This is an industry-wide problem in AI, not just in manufacturing. Look at health care. Every hospital has its own slightly different format for electronic health records. How can every hospital train its own custom AI model? Expecting every hospital’s IT personnel to invent new neural-network architectures is unrealistic. The only way out of this dilemma is to build tools that empower the customers to build their own models by giving them tools to engineer the data and express their domain knowledge. That’s what Landing AI is executing in computer vision, and the field of AI needs other teams to execute this in other domains.

Is there anything else you think it’s important for people to understand about the work you’re doing or the data-centric AI movement?

Industry observers note that ng: In the last decade, the biggest shift in AI was a shift to deep learning. I think it’s quite possible that in this decade the biggest shift will be to data-centric AI. With the maturity of today’s neural network architectures, I think for a lot of the practical applications the bottleneck will be whether we can efficiently get the data we need to develop systems that work well. The data-centric AI movement has tremendous energy and momentum across the whole community. I hope more researchers and developers will jump in and work on it.

This article appears in the April 2022 print matter as “Andrew Ng, AI Minimalist.”.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Five major tech outages in quick succession earlier this month led to speculation that they were connected, with some inevitably believing them to be AI-related.
  • That wasn’t the case, but the US Director of National Intelligence is one of a number of experts warning that we should expect AI-powered outages in the near future ….
  • Sources indicate that earlier this month saw five tech outages, one after the other.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Five major tech outages in quick succession earlier this month led to speculation that they were connected, with some inevitably believing them to be AI-related.

That wasn’t the case, but the US Director of National Intelligence is one of a number of experts warning that we should expect AI-powered outages in the near future ….

Sources indicate that earlier this month saw five tech outages, one after the other. A widespread Microsoft 365 outage occurred when two unrelated concerns coincided. The next day saw a nationwide ground stop of US air traffic due to a communication issue affecting all air traffic control centers. A few days later, a bug in a Chase bank system saw disruption not only to the bank itself, but also other banks where Chase was a party to a transaction. Many Apple services went offline later the same week, with retail stores also affected. Finally, United Airlines had its own widespread IT outage that grounded a significant number of flights.

Each had their own unrelated causes, with the White House stating that rumors of an AI-facilitated systemic attack by a hostile state were false.

Recent findings suggest that however, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has warned that we should expect future tech outages as a result of attacks facilitated by AI-discovered vulnerabilities. CNBC reports him issuing the warning on CNN’s State of the Union.

The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road.

You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot.

We already saw an example of this last month when a vulnerability discovered in PHP saw a significant number of websites being taken offline.

Microsoft President Brad Smith says it isn’t just a question of bad actors exploiting vulnerabilities discovered by AI, but companies rushing to patch these may inadvertently cause systems to fail, as Newsweek reports.

What AI did earlier this year was basically make it much easier for people to find vulnerabilities in code, and then you can either use that knowledge to patch the code, or if you’re a bad actor, you can use that knowledge to try to hack into systems.

Especially when you have older infrastructure, especially when you’re trying to patch at such a pace, especially when you have to go so fast that you can’t take as much time to test what you’re changing in the code, you do increase the risk of something going wrong.

Major IT failures look set to be a routine event in the coming weeks and months.

#120766. 12 Things to Do on Christmas If You Don’t Celebrate

12 Things to Do on Christmas If You Don’t Celebrate

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1037 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it.
  • You can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex.
  • If Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it. You get to enjoy all the brightly colored lights your neighbors put up, but you don’t have to put up your own. You don’t have to do any duty-shopping. There's no pressure. But Christmas Day itself leaves you in a mostly shuttered world that feels like there’s nothing going on. Fortunately, there are options to make Dec. 25 a fun day off, regardless of your observances.

You can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex. Chinese restaurants and movie theaters traditionally stay open on Christmas Day for those who don't celebrate, and they’re often filled with fellow Christmas refugees. Check Google for the hours of your local Chinese restaurant and give them a call to make a reservation. If you’re more adventurous and you’re in a city large enough to have a Chinatown (or a whatever-town), just head straight there on Christmas and see what happens—that’s how the best days usually start.

If Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses. Just make sure you check first. Lots of chain restaurants are open on Christmas Day too, including Applebee's, McDonald’s, Benihana, and more. You can even get Christmas breakfast at your local IHOP. But not every location of every outlet follows the same hours.

Recent findings suggest that as for movies, most chain multiplex theaters are open on Dec. 25, and theaters are usually pretty full. The movies attract both people who don't celebrate Christmas and people who do, but want to get away from their families for a couple hours, so make sure and reserve a seat beforehand. Consider hitting up an out-of-the-way spot or that theater with the table service and cushy recliners to make it feel like more of an occasion.

Most people going to the movies on Christmas Day aren’t there for Christmas movies, so interesting “secular” movies are often slated for release on the 25th. This year's Christmas is unusually packed with interesting new movies, including family flick Jumani: Open World, a Robert Eggers horror movie called Werwulf, and the crowd pleasing football story Mr. Irrelevant, so you have serious options.

Chinese restaurants and movie theaters aren’t the only establishments open on Christmas. Here are some other options:.

Industry observers note that go skiing or snowboarding: Most mountains are open on Christmas, and the lift lines are blissfully empty. There's no better way of celebrating a winter-based holiday than on a wide-open mountain.

Visit a skating rink: Speaking of winter sports, ice skating rinks are generally open on Christmas too.

Pretend to be a tourist: Tourist attractions are often open on Christmas, especially in larger cities. This includes places like Madame Tussaud’s and Ripley’s Believe It or Not, as well as ziplines and Segway tours—so do that touristy thing you’ve never done before.

According to recent reports, get a room: If you’ve got some spare cash and have nothing better to do, get a room at a hotel. Hotels don’t usually close on Christmas, and they typically offer plenty of amenities, so take advantage of the pool at the Holiday Inn or the spa at the Four Seasons, depending on your lifestyle.

Recent findings suggest that hiking and biking: Hiking trails and parks are open on Christmas if you want to get outdoors. If you’re into biking, hit the trails or hit the streets: Traffic is minimal on Christmas, so it’s a great time to put in some serious roadwork.

Volunteer: Not having anything to do on Christmas isn’t the biggest life problem, especially compared to people who have nowhere to go and nothing to eat. So use Christmas to help people and actually deliver on that whole “good will towards men” thing. Check your local Craigslist for volunteering opportunities.

Recent findings suggest that use Christmas as a catch-up day: This is strictly for type-A people, but if everyone is out of town and no one is going to call you, why not spend the day catching up on neglected chores or personal projects? You can spend at least part of your day knocking a few things off your to-do list and the rest of the time relaxing. That way you’ll get a break and still feel accomplished.

Just sleep all day: Type-B personalities like me see a day free of obligations and other people as a golden opportunity to do as little as is humanly possible, a day to fully commit to sloth.

In a recent development, spend time with friends and family at home: Not celebrating Christmas doesn’t mean you can’t spend the day with family and/or friends. Get together with your loved ones, play games, watch a movie, cook together, talk, or whatever else you all enjoy. You don’t have to go out to have fun, so don’t rule out staying in with people you care about.

Recent findings suggest that shopping: This is at the bottom of the list because it’s iffy. Drug stores and convenience stores like 711 are usually open on the 25th. Grocery chains like Kroger’s and Trader Joe’s usually aren’t. Your local shopping mall or retail district might be open, but probably won't be, so check ahead.

Because so many places are closed on Christmas Day, you should plan ahead (unless you like spontaneity and are OK with the possibility of disappointment) by:.

Making a list of the places you want to go.

Calling nearby locations to confirm they’ll be open, as not every chain follows corporate holiday hour recommendations.

Making reservations at any restaurant(s) you proposal to visit.

Putting together a basic timeline of the day, accounting for travel time, so you don’t lose any reservations, miss a movie, or arrive after the store closes.

In a recent development, the most crucial advice here is to do something intentional on Christmas, even if it's sleeping in, so the day doesn't feel depressing or empty. So hit the slopes, suck down some dim sum, or keep your couch from floating away, but be sure you make Christmas your own.

Tech Report: Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia, stock up 30%

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia has announced that disgraced CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated to the role, effective immediately.
  • It said that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so ….
  • Huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy became the main headline news in the tech press after coming to light at the end of last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia has announced that disgraced CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated to the role, effective immediately. The tech giant’s share price jumped more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also making significant gains.

It said that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so ….

Huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy became the main headline news in the tech press after coming to light at the end of last month. The Newly introduced York Times broke the story on October 29, citing it then as “a close relationship.” Nvidia initially denied that the relationship was anything out of the ordinary.

That changed on November 8 when Huang publicly admitted to the affair. Nvidia’s shares dropped 5%, and the manufacturer’s board of directors opened an independent investigation. Further details emerged over the following days. Things got even worse when the same paper reported that Huang had also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him.

That led to Huang being fired resigning on November 12.

He won’t make that mistake again!

Recent findings suggest that despite putting the firm at enormous risk and initially lying to its board of directors, there were calls in some quarters for Huang to be reinstated. He responded by saying that he would be “honored” to return if asked to do so.

The board of directors, however, said that it had no intention of inviting him back.

Nvidia’s chair Harvey Jones mentioned: “The board does not intend to reinstate him.”.

That changed today, with the manufacturer making the announcement in a press release.

Recent findings suggest that nvidia today declared that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” mentioned Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a fresh industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”.

As previously confirmed, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

Advances in sensing, manufacturing, computational resources, and data-driven methods are enabling new approaches to electromagnetic sensing, non-destructive evaluation, and advanced materials processing. This webinar will demonstrate how the COMSOL Multiphysics software supports predictive modeling by coupling electromagnetic fields with thermal, chemical, mechanical, and transport phenomena across multiple length and time scales.The first application we will show focuses on eddy-current thermometry for reconstructing three-dimensional temperature fields in metal plates. Temperature-dependent electrical conductivity alters induced currents and magnetic fields, enabling volumetric thermal inference. COMSOL simulations of defects and laser-induced transient heating will support validation of reconstruction algorithms. Multifrequency excitation will be investigated to improve depth discrimination through frequency-dependent penetration depths and sensitivities.The second application examines microwave-enabled volumetric additive manufacturing of ceramic components. A high-power microwave beamforming array delivers localized energy into three-dimensional volumes, enabling processing of opaque, particle-laden resins. Coupled COMSOL models of electromagnetic propagation, microwave absorption, heat transfer, and ceramic sintering kinetics are used to predict temperature evolution, reaction progression, spatial resolution, and processing scalability. Future extensions will incorporate pulsed excitation, fluid flow, resin viscosity, convection, shrinkage, and solid mechanics.Together, these examples demonstrate how the COMSOL software can integrate multiphysics modeling with sensing, manufacturing, and data inversion. This webinar will present two applications of coupled electromagnetic and thermal modeling in COMSOL Multiphysics: eddy-current thermometry in metal plates and microwave-assisted processing of ceramic-loaded resins. By connecting simulation with practical engineering systems, COMSOL-based modeling can accelerate technology development, reduce experimental iteration, and support reliable scale-up of next-generation electromagnetic technologies. 💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, last week, OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2, its latest generation of AI models, with some impressive capabilities for coding, research and tackling complex projects. But for those of us who use ChatGPT for everything from planning dinner to troubleshooting tech problems, this week's update might be even more useful.

OpenAI is bringing a version of GPT-6.2 Sol to the regular Chat tab, so you no longer need to switch to ChatGPT Work to benefit from some of the manufacturer's latest AI improvements.

According to OpenAI's release notes, ChatGPT is now better at making sense of images, handling complicated requests and searching the web. It can also recognize when you might benefit from a little extra help, such as keeping an eye on the price of a product you've been meaning to buy.

It has been revealed that one of the biggest improvements is how well ChatGPT understands images. In OpenAI's internal testing, GPT-6.2 scored 71.7%, up from 47.4% with GPT-6. It also handled particularly challenging instructions with a 78.1% success rate, compared with 62.5% for the previous model.

Benchmarks are one thing, but I'm more interested in what these improvements mean when you're using ChatGPT in your everyday life.

Here are five prompts worth trying.

One of the most frustrating things about using AI to organize your life is when it overlooks an notable detail. You might give ChatGPT a dozen things you need to accomplish, only to discover that its carefully organized schedule doesn't account for travel time or the fact that you need to be in two places at once.

Sources indicate that GPT-6.2's improved instruction following could make it more reliable when juggling competing priorities. The key is to give ChatGPT multiple constraints that require it to think through the problem rather than simply organize a list.

Recent findings suggest that try this prompt: Help me organize Thanksgiving morning. Dinner is at 3 p.m., my turkey needs four hours in the oven and 30 minutes to rest, my sides need different oven temperatures and I need an hour to get ready. Create a realistic schedule, flag any conflicts and build in extra time in case something goes wrong.

ChatGPT has been able to analyze photos for years, but its ability to interpret smaller details and understand how objects relate to one another hasn't always been consistent.

Sources indicate that with the latest upgrade, it's worth revisiting some of the visual tasks that may have disappointed you in the past. Take a picture of a cluttered kitchen cabinet, your refrigerator or even the tangled cables behind your TV.

Sources indicate that try this prompt: Analyze this photo and identify three changes I could make to improve this space without buying anything newly introduced. Base your suggestions only on what you can actually see, and tell me if you're uncertain about anything.

With Black Friday deals already happening now, the timing of ChatGPT's improved web research capabilities couldn't be better.

Instead of asking the chatbot to find the cheapest version of a product, give it a more complicated shopping decision that requires it to weigh several factors.A useful response should go beyond rounding up products. It should explain why certain features matter for your particular home and whether spending more would actually make a difference.

Remember to verify prices and availability before making a purchase.

Industry observers note that try this prompt: Find the three best robot vacuum deals at the moment available for under $300. I have pets, hardwood floors and several area rugs. Prioritize obstacle avoidance and pet hair pickup over flashy features. Check current prices, compare independent reviews and explain which one offers the best value. Include links to your sources.

You don't always need AI to write something from scratch. Sometimes, the more valuable skill is its ability to understand exactly what you want changed without touching everything else.

The improvements to GPT-6.2's instruction following could be useful for anyone who has asked ChatGPT to make a minor edit, only to receive a completely rewritten document.

Recent findings suggest that paste in an email, holiday letter or piece of writing you've been working on. This is a surprisingly demanding task for an AI model because it requires restraint as much as writing ability.

Try this prompt: Edit this for clarity without changing my personality or writing style. Keep my opening and closing sentences exactly as they are. Don't add fresh information, don't make it more formal and don't rewrite sentences that already work. Show me the revised version and briefly explain your three most significant changes.

One of the more interesting improvements in this update has less to do with the quality of ChatGPT's immediate answers and more to do with what happens after the conversation.

Industry observers note that openAI claims the chatbot is better at identifying situations where ongoing assistance might be useful. For example, instead of repeatedly checking whether a product has gone on sale, you could ask ChatGPT to monitor it. Depending on your account's available features, ChatGPT may offer to set up an automated price check. Make sure you confirm that the task has actually been created rather than assuming the chatbot will continue monitoring something on its own.

Industry observers note that try this prompt: I'm interested in buying a Kindle Scribe, but I don't want to pay full price. Find the best available deal today and offer to notify me if the price drops below $250 before Christmas.

With the newest upgrade, OpenAI is focusing on some of the everyday frustrations that can make AI feel like more work than it's worth.

Having to repeat instructions, correct misunderstood images or double-check research can quickly undermine the time-saving benefits of using an AI assistant.

If GPT-6.2 can reduce those frustrations, this upgrade could be a productivity improvement for the average ChatGPT user.

Watching a movie on your iPhone is convenient, but craning your neck for a comfortable view is hardly cinematic. Having a premium AR display in sunglasses form, without packing a bulky mixed-reality headset or computing puck, opens up entirely new possibilities.

The RayNeo GT Max and RayNeo GT connect to your device over a single USB-C cable. Instead of clunky goggles, the GT Series puts a massive virtual display — 59 degrees of field of view on GT Max, to be exact — into a sleek, understated sunglasses design that blends into coffee shops and airport lounges at just 68 to 78 grams. That single USB-C connection carries uncompressed video and powers the glasses directly: no secondary battery packs to carry, no charging anxiety, and zero wireless lag.

In a recent development, one thing to check before you buy: the glasses need a device that outputs video over USB-C (DisplayPort Alt Mode). That covers the iPhone 15, 16 and 17 series, Macs from 2015 onward with USB-C, iPad from the 10th generation on, and USB-C handhelds like the Steam Deck. The iPhone 16e, 17e and iPhone Air have USB-C ports but don’t output video over them, so they aren’t supported. Consoles and older Lightning devices need RayNeo’s HDMI adapter.

Both GT Max and GT use dual 1080p Micro-OLED panels, delivering a Full HD image to each eye with ultra-smooth 120Hz refresh rates in 2D mode. GT Max adds 38 pixels per degree, 98% DCI-P3 cinematic color coverage, and TÜV Rheinland triple eye-comfort certification. Each model offers three selectable virtual screen sizes, depending on how immersed you want to be:.

Recent findings suggest that GT Max’s wider field of view provides a more expansive picture, while GT offers a featherweight design. For travel, the appeal is simple: an immaculate 307-inch personal theater that slips right into your daily bag alongside your Apple gear.

It has been revealed that the GT Series also functions as an instant, private external display for a USB-C Mac. That makes the glasses invaluable far beyond streaming media, especially when you need an expansive, shoulder-surfer-proof dual-monitor workspace on a flight, train, or co-working desk.

Both GT and GT Max include three native 3DoF hardware display modes, meaning you can position your virtual screen around your head:.

It has been revealed that because the tracking runs on dedicated silicon inside the glasses, none of it taxes the Mac or iPhone you’re plugged into. The glasses draw minimal power directly from the connected device and include a four-speaker spatial acoustic array co-tuned by Bang & Olufsen, with a directional Whisper Mode that cuts sound leakage on a plane or in an office.

GT Max also comes in three sizes based on inter-pupillary distance (IPD) — small for under 64mm, medium for 64–67mm, large for over 67mm — ensuring a tailored, comfortable fit.

In a recent development, if an everyday display frame came out of Cupertino today, it would look like RayNeo iO. Rather than heavy visors, iO pairs with your iPhone through the RayNeo app to project glanceable, contextual intelligence into genuine everyday eyewear.

The waveguide is 97% transparent and the optical engine is hidden inside the frame, so from the outside these read as ordinary glasses — most people never clock them as smart eyewear at all.

For presentations and pitches, the built-in teleprompter scrolls your notes in sync with your natural speaking cadence, so you keep your eyes locked on your audience instead of looking down at your phone. Sources indicate that rayNeo iO’s productivity tools extend that concept further with a focus on personal privacy. This is where they really shine in the Apple ecosystem. A four-microphone array with a bone-conduction sensor captures clear audio for automated meeting minutes and AI summaries that extract key action items. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.
  • The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.
  • Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

Sources indicate that ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

Arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

Champions 🏆 pic.twitter.com/c0IVLYu3fB.

Arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀.

When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

Sources indicate that the Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Recent findings suggest that yesterday Arsenal revealed the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:.

Industry observers note that “I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a newly introduced challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very key and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”.

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the newly introduced season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

It has been revealed that arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

Industry observers note that “I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

Sources indicate that “I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”.

Recent findings suggest that this is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Sources indicate that dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

10 Hidden Controls Every 'GTA 6' Player Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (816 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that you can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests.
  • If you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode.
  • Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that you can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests. However, if you take a minute to learn a few hidden controls, I think you'll enjoy the game even more. These are fairly simple controls that let you hide from the cops, trash talk other drivers, or flip the bird when you're feeling like annoying NPCs. These are 10 of the best hidden GTA 6 controls that'll help you unlock an entirely newly introduced side of the game.

If you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode. It's a relaxing way to enjoy the streets without having to worry about following traffic rules. To enable it, you need to get in a vehicle and add a waypoint on the map. This serves as your character's destination, so if you want a longer drive, be sure to drop the waypoint far, far away. Next, hold the down arrow on the D-Pad, and press the Option button. This enables cinematic mode. Then, hold the Circle button to enable auto-drive.

Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6. When this happens, you attract heat, and soon enough, cops will begin chasing you. Switching cars is a great way to reduce the amount of attention you get from law enforcement, but you can still be identified by your face or clothing. Until you can reach a safe spot to swap outfits, maintain a low profile by ducking while driving. Hold the Circle button while driving to duck.

EA's Road Rash was among the first racing games I played as a child, and I remember how much fun it was to kick your rivals while speeding through the game's various courses. You can have a taste of that in GTA 6 too. Press the Square button while you're riding a bike, and your character will kick anyone who's near you. If you do this in a car, it opens the door, and hits people around the car. To annoy other drivers, press R3, and your character will direct some trash talk towards NPCs.

Sources indicate that hold Circle to lean back against walls, or to sit on the beach. To rest on a ledge, you can hold L3. This lets you take a moment to soak in beautiful views in the game, or lounge around as you listen to NPC conversations. Paying attention to those conversations can lead to some fun side quests, and sometimes give you a tip or two for quick money or other rewards.

If you really want to rile people up in GTA 6, you can flip the bird. This works only when your character is unarmed. Hold L2, focus on a person, then press R1. Actions have consequences in GTA 6, so be prepared to fight NPCs when you do this.

Sources indicate that when you're being chased by cops, enemies, or angry NPCs, you can use a quick shortcut to look back without turning the camera around. Just hold R3 to look behind you.

Sources indicate that while driving, press Circle to toggle headlights (and switch to high beams). This is particularly useful when you're offroading at night. You can also hold left arrow on the D-Pad, and move the right stick up to access other vehicle controls like hazard lights, opening or closing windows, etc., in case you want to add to the realism.

Stealing emergency vehicles in GTA 6 is risky, but the reward is totally worth it. Not only do you find stashes of weapons, gear, and money in some of these vehicles, but you also have access to sirens that help you clear traffic off your path. If you steal an ambulance or a cop car, hold L3, and move the left stick up to go through different siren tones. Press L3 and the left stick up to enable the siren.

GTA 6 is a third-person game, but it has a first-person mode that partially works. It is useful for looking at smaller objects around your character, such as posters, small signs, or to look for clues in and around a house. (Yes, I am talking about Mandy's creepy house and bad vibes.) Hold L2 + hit R3 to switch to first-person mode. Sadly, you can't move when you do this, but you can look around. Try it in Mandy's property to observe a few nasty surprises.

Industry observers note that when you sprint towards a car, press the X button to slide across the hood. This is much faster and smoother than running around parked cars or jumping over them. It also looks cool, which is reason enough to try this feature.

  • Recent findings suggest that apple’s environmental record isn’t entirely perfect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I think Apple can reasonably claim to be the leading tech giant when it comes to its environmental credentials. It has led the way with its use of renewable energy, made significant strides with carbon-neutral production, and removed plastic from all its packaging.

All of this could potentially be put at risk by the company’s ambitions for Siri AI, however, as Meta joins Google in admitting it is now unlikely to meet its own 2030 net zero promise, thanks to the huge power demands of the data centers powering its AI services ….

Recent findings suggest that apple’s environmental record isn’t entirely perfect. For example, when it claimed that the Apple Watch Series 9 and Ultra 2 were carbon neutral back in 2023, that claim was described as “bogus,” with the EU banning Apple from repeating it. The tech giant has also been criticized for pushing a relentless annual iPhone cycle, encouraging frequent upgrades.

Sources indicate that overall, however, Apple has first-rate credentials when it comes to the environment. It was way back in 2018 when the manufacturer hit its goal of running its own operations off 100% renewable energy. This includes all Apple facilities, from Apple Park through data centers to its worldwide retail store network.

I remarked at the time that using more environmentally friendly packaging should be the tech giant’s next priority, and it has indeed made great progress with this over the years, succeeding in removing all plastic packaging earlier this year.

After its own operations, Apple set about trying to tackle the power usage of its manufacturing partners. Back in 2020, the tech giant set a goal of having its entire supply chain be carbon neutral by 2030. Just four years later, Apple said it was 95% of the way there.

The firm also helps fund and support a wide range of environmental initiatives around the world. Just a few examples include conservation in China’s national parks, environmental protection and carbon removal in Australia and Upcoming Zealand, and helping to fund the build-out of renewable energy capacity in India.

Potentially, however, the vast energy demands of the data centers powering AI services could put its 2030 goal at risk. Other tech giants have already admitted that it may lead them to fail to hit their own renewable energy promises.

According to recent reports, back in 2024, for example, Google CEO Sundar Pichai said that the AI boom was “challenging” to the company’s 2030 carbon-free goal. CNET reports that Meta is now also admitting that it may fail to hit the same target.

Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the organization is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline.”.

Notably, a lot of Siri’s most advanced AI capabilities are currently powered by Google’s Gemini models.

It has been revealed that at the same 2024 event where Google expressed doubts, Apple reiterated its commitment to its 2030 target. Then-CEO Tim Cook repeated this assurance later the same year, although admitted it would be challenging.

More challenges, yes. But are we coming off the goal? No, definitely not. With more data centers, you use more renewable energy, and we’ve built that muscle now […] I feel very good about 2030.

In the firm’s most recent environmental progress report, it said that it was was still using 100% renewable energy despite using over 2.5 billion kWh of electricity to power its data centers.

According to recent reports, we’re proud that 100 percent of that electricity came from renewable sources including solar, wind, and low-impact hydropower. To cover our needs, we build our own renewable power projects and work with utilities to purchase clean energy from locally obtained resources. We’re staying at 100 percent even as Apple’s data center capacity continues to grow.

The same report stated the tech giant had achieved zero water use for cooling at its latest data centers.

At our three newest data centers, we use high-efficiency air-cooled chillers instead of water-cooled systems, resulting in zero water use for cooling.

However, the greatest challenge for Apple lies ahead. The reason that Google and Meta are now backtracking on their promises is that both companies now have massive AI capabilities. As yet, Apple does not.

It has been revealed that what happens as Apple expands Siri AI capabilities as usage increases, and as the company moves into agentic AI features? Is it realistic for the company to maintain its 100% track record with vastly greater data center energy usage?

Greenpeace expressed its own doubts earlier this year.

“AI will be the defining test of Apple’s climate commitments,” spokesperson Avex Li says. “To preserve Tim Cook’s environmental legacy, the organization will need to show that AI growth can be accommodated within its existing climate commitments through absolute emissions reductions, additional renewable energy investment, and longer-lasting products.”.

Apple did not respond directly but merely pointed to its past statements and most recent environmental progress report.

I don’t doubt the firm’s desire to maintain its track record, but if Apple does join the likes of Google and Meta in becoming a major AI player, sticking to its 2030 timing is going to become increasingly difficult.

Sources indicate that do you think Apple will succeed? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

Ah, the Bulgarian split squat. Feared by many, loathed by most, but loved by personal trainers all over the world. What if I told you that you'd enjoy this lower-body exercise infinitely more if you followed three simple steps to fix up your form?

It's surprisingly easy to make mistakes with this leg-day exercise, and really, it can be adjusted to be more quad-dominant or glute-dominant — but there are clear signs of bad form, and many more people than you'd think end up on the physical therapy couch because of poor lifting mechanics.

To maximize the benefits of this weightlifting exercise, I recommend learning how to do the Bulgarian split squat before bad habits set in. As a trainer, I have a few tips to help you. Scroll on to see if you're making these common mistakes below and my top tips to fix your form fast.

A post shared by Tom's Guide Fitness | Workout Tips & Gear (@tomsguidefitness).

It's a compound exercise and a part of functional training workouts and strength programs everywhere, helping you build strength and muscle in your glutes, hips, quads, hamstrings and core.

The move requires balance and coordination, while your upper body, core and hips help stabilize you as you move. But people tend to think of this move as more quads than glutes, which isn't exactly the case.

Here's what I see go wrong, and three quick fixes:.

Sources indicate that in short, you're wasting your time if your form is badly off. And we're busy humans who don't like our time being wasted, right?

It has been revealed that leaning back too far removes tension from the working muscles and overloads your lower back. Keep your torso static and stable — don't hunch or allow your knees to cave inward. That means engaging your core and using the power of your core, glutes and legs to drive movement.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Next, think about your gravity; as I mentioned, keep your back straight and slightly hinge forward to help engage the glutes on your standing leg. If you work with a weight in your opposite hand, this will engage more of the outer glutes, or gluteus medius.

Taking time during the eccentric contraction means slowing down the lowering phase; you can then press upward with power while maximizing tension. It's now thought, due to advances in research, that eccentric contraction is important for muscle growth and braking force.

If you have an injury, pre-existing health conditions, or you experience pain, speak with a qualified personal trainer or physician first.
